passages.title: The Lord’s preface warns the world and vouches for his servants
passages.setting: Joseph Smith received this revelation on 1 November 1831 at Hiram, Ohio, during a conference of elders. The elders had met to plan a published book of his revelations, the Book of Commandments. Minutes say the revelation came during a break between the conference sessions. William McLellin later recalled that the conference rejected a preface drafted by Oliver Cowdery, Sidney Rigdon, and McLellin himself. According to McLellin, Joseph then dictated this preface a few sentences at a time while Rigdon wrote.
passages.summary: The revelation opens with a voice calling all people, near and far, to listen. It says disciples chosen in the last days will carry a warning to everyone. It calls itself the Lord’s preface to the book of his commandments. It charges that people have strayed from God’s ordinances and broken his everlasting covenant. It says the Lord, knowing the coming calamity, called Joseph Smith so that “the weak and the simple” could proclaim the gospel. It says the commandments came to servants in their weakness, so their errors could be corrected and their humility rewarded. It calls the church “the only true and living church” and promises forgiveness to those who repent. It ends by telling readers to search these commandments, which it says will all be fulfilled.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson on section 1 teaches that the Lord uses “the weak and the simple” to do his work. In verses 24–28, what four outcomes does the Lord promise for servants who err, seek wisdom, sin, or are humble?

contextNote.title: Why publish revelations given to weak men
contextNote.text: A book of revelations faced an obvious objection: the men who received them were ordinary and flawed. Verse 24 answers it directly. It says the commandments came “in their weakness, after the manner of their language” so servants could understand. Verses 25–28 then list the purpose: errors made known, sinners chastened, the humble made strong. Verse 38 states the other side: the word is “the same” whether the Lord or his servants speak it. In this preface, the servants’ weakness is part of how the revelations came, not a flaw the book hides.

passages.title: Elijah will turn children’s hearts to their fathers before the Lord comes
passages.setting: Section 2 is not a separate revelation text but an excerpt from Joseph Smith’s history. It records words Joseph reported hearing from a heavenly messenger on the night of 21 September 1823, when he was 17. The visit took place in the Smith family’s log home near Palmyra, New York. The official heading identifies the messenger as Moroni, the last keeper of the records that became the Book of Mormon. The messenger quoted Malachi 4:5–6 in a form that differs from the King James Bible. Joseph’s history was written from 1838 on, and these verses joined the Doctrine and Covenants in 1876.
passages.summary: The messenger speaks for the Lord in three short verses. First, the Lord will reveal the priesthood by the hand of Elijah the prophet. This will happen before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah will plant in the children’s hearts the promises made to the fathers. Then the hearts of the children will turn to their fathers. If this did not happen, the whole earth would be utterly wasted at the Lord’s coming.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 2 teaches that the Lord sent Elijah to turn our hearts to our ancestors. Which “promises made to the fathers” in verse 2 might you trace in your own family’s history?

contextNote.title: What turns the children’s hearts
contextNote.text: In the King James Bible, Malachi says Elijah will turn hearts between fathers and children. Verse 2 adds a step before the turning. Elijah will first “plant in the hearts of the children” the promises made to the fathers. The children turn because those promises have been placed in them. Verse 1 ties this work to priesthood revealed by Elijah’s hand. Verse 3 gives the stakes: without it, the earth would be “utterly wasted” at the Lord’s coming. Here, turning the heart means taking the fathers’ promises as one’s own.

passages.title: God’s work cannot be frustrated, but Joseph can still fall
passages.setting: From April to June 1828, Joseph Smith dictated the first Book of Mormon manuscript at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Martin Harris as scribe. Harris pressed to take the 116 pages home to Palmyra, New York, and Joseph finally agreed. Soon after, Emma Smith gave birth to a son who did not survive, and Joseph cared for her for weeks. In early July he went to Palmyra and learned the pages were lost. Joseph’s history says he received this revelation through the Urim and Thummim after returning to Harmony. It is the earliest of his revelations with a surviving text.
passages.summary: The revelation begins by declaring that God’s works and purposes cannot be frustrated. It is the work of men that fails, especially those who boast in their own strength. It then turns to Joseph and recalls how strict his commandments were. It says he gave in to the persuasions of men and feared man more than God. If Joseph repents, he is still chosen; if not, he will lose his gift. He lost his privileges for handing sacred things to a wicked man. Still, the revelation says, the work will go forth. It says the plates were preserved so the Lamanites might know the promises made to their fathers and believe in Christ.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 draws from this section the teaching that we can trust God. According to verses 7–8, what would God have done for Joseph if he had stayed faithful under pressure?

contextNote.title: Whose work failed
contextNote.text: The lost pages could look like a failure of God’s plan. Verse 3 says the failure belongs to “the work of men,” not to the work of God. Verse 4 describes how a man falls, through boasting and following his own will. Verses 6–7 say Joseph had “gone on in the persuasions of men” and feared man more than God. Verse 10 keeps the door open: if he repents, he is “still chosen” for the work. Verse 16 then repeats the opening claim that “my work shall go forth” despite the loss. In this revelation, frustrated work belongs to people who stop following God’s counsel, not to God.

passages.title: Desire to serve is the first qualification for the work
passages.setting: Joseph Smith Sr. visited his son at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in early 1829. Joseph had apparently not translated the plates since the lost manuscript of June 1828. He dictated this revelation for his father shortly before translation began again. A scribe later corrected the date in Revelation Book 1 from 1828 to 1829.
passages.summary: The revelation announces that a marvelous work is about to come forth. It tells those who enter God’s service to serve with heart, might, mind, and strength. Then it says that desire to serve is itself a call to the work. It compares the moment to a field ready for harvest. The worker who reaps with energy also gains salvation. It lists faith, hope, charity, and love as the qualities that fit a person for the work. It ends with a list of ten virtues and the promise to ask and receive.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 treats this revelation as a call to anyone willing to serve. Which of the qualities in verses 5–6 could you develop this week, and how?

contextNote.title: A call that begins with wanting to serve
contextNote.text: Joseph Smith Sr. held no office when this revelation came. Verse 3 makes desire the starting point: if you want to serve, you are called. Verse 2 then sets the standard for that service: all heart, might, mind, and strength. Verse 4 explains the urgency with a harvest image. A ripe field will not wait for a better season. Verse 5 names what qualifies the worker, and none of it is rank or training. In this text, a call is first a willingness that God then shapes.

passages.title: Three witnesses will see the plates, but humility comes first
passages.setting: Martin Harris traveled to Harmony, Pennsylvania, in March 1829. There is no record that he and Joseph Smith had met since the manuscript was lost in 1828. Around Palmyra, opposition to the plates was growing, and Harris’s wife Lucy led much of it. She filed a complaint before a magistrate in Lyons, New York, alleging fraud. Harris came wanting a further witness that Joseph truly had the plates, and this revelation answered his request.
passages.summary: The revelation answers Martin Harris’s wish for a witness that Joseph had the plates. It says Joseph covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord names. His first gift is to translate, and he should claim no other until that is finished. If people will not believe God’s words, they would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. It promises three witnesses who will be shown the plates by God’s power. Joseph is told to repent and to yield to the persuasions of men no more. Harris can be a witness if he humbles himself in mighty prayer and faith; then he may only say he has seen them. If Harris does not humble himself, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then stop until commanded again.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 teaches that through the Holy Ghost we can gain a witness of the Book of Mormon. Compare verses 16 and 24: what does each say a person must do before receiving a witness?

contextNote.title: Why Martin Harris had to wait
contextNote.text: Martin Harris wanted proof that the plates were real. Verse 24 names what stood in his way: he “exalts himself and does not humble himself sufficiently” before God. The condition it sets is humility in “mighty prayer and faith,” not a better argument. Verse 7 explains why a display alone would not work. People who reject God’s words would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. Verse 28 states the reverse: without humility, Harris will have “no such views” at all. In this revelation, a witness is a view granted to the humble, not evidence handed to a doubter.

passages.title: Oliver Cowdery already had a witness: peace from God
passages.setting: Oliver Cowdery had boarded with Joseph Smith’s parents near Palmyra, New York. Joseph’s history says Oliver prayed there about the plates and received a confirmation. He arrived in Harmony, Pennsylvania, on 5 April 1829 and began writing as Joseph translated two days later. Some time after, Joseph dictated this revelation, which the heading says came through the Urim and Thummim. It seems to have answered questions Oliver had not voiced to Joseph.
passages.summary: The revelation announces a marvelous work and calls anyone who desires to reap in a ripe field. It tells Oliver to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It tells him to stand by Joseph, to admonish him, and to accept admonition from him. It reminds him that each time he inquired, the Spirit instructed him. It points him to a night when he prayed and received peace in his mind. It offers him a gift to translate, like Joseph, and gives both of them the keys of this gift. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice tells them to fear not and do good. It ends by asking them to look to him in every thought and behold his wounds.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 6–9 teaches that Heavenly Father speaks to us through the Holy Ghost. In verses 14–16 and 22–23, what forms did the Lord’s answers to Oliver take?

contextNote.title: A witness Oliver had already received
contextNote.text: Oliver wanted more assurance that the work was true. Verse 22 sends him back to the night he “cried unto me in your heart” for an answer. Verse 23 then asks what greater witness he could have than peace from God. Verse 24 adds a second sign: the revelation told him “things which no man knoweth” about himself. David Whitmer later recalled Oliver writing that Joseph had revealed things only God could know. In this section, a witness is peace spoken to the mind, confirmed by private knowledge.

passages.title: John chose to stay and serve until Christ returns
passages.setting: In April 1829, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. They disagreed over whether the apostle John had died or remained on earth. John 21 raises the question but does not settle it. Joseph’s history says they agreed to ask through the Urim and Thummim. Joseph’s history calls it a translation of a parchment John wrote and hid. No account says Joseph had the parchment itself.
passages.summary: The text is written in John’s own voice. The Lord asks John what he desires, and John asks for power over death to bring souls to Christ. The Lord promises that John will tarry until the Lord comes in glory. The Lord then explains to Peter why John will remain. Peter desired to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom, and that was a good desire. John desired a greater work among men, so the Lord will make him “as flaming fire and a ministering angel” for the heirs of salvation. Peter will minister for John and James, and the three will hold the keys of this ministry. Both men receive what they desired.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson pairs section 7 with the promise “even as you desire of me so it shall be” in section 6. What did John and Peter each desire in verses 2 and 4, and what does verse 8 say about both?

contextNote.title: Why John did not die
contextNote.text: John 21 left readers unsure whether Jesus said John would not die. Verse 3 answers directly that John will “tarry until I come in my glory” and prophesy to nations. The reason is John’s own request in verse 2, for power over death to bring souls to Christ. Verses 4–5 contrast Peter, who wanted to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom. The Lord calls Peter’s desire good and John’s a greater work. Verse 8 grants each man what he wanted. In this account, to “tarry” means to keep working among people, not merely to live long.

passages.title: Revelation comes to the mind and heart by the Holy Ghost
passages.setting: Oliver Cowdery began writing for Joseph Smith at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in April 1829. An earlier revelation, now section 6, had offered him a gift to translate. Oliver wanted that power, and this revelation answered his request. In the earliest copy, his second gift is called working with the “sprout,” or rod. Many people then used such rods to search for water or minerals. Later editions call it the gift of Aaron.
passages.summary: The revelation promises Oliver Cowdery knowledge of whatever he asks in faith with an honest heart. It applies this to the engravings of ancient records. It says the Lord will speak to his mind and heart by the Holy Ghost. It calls this the spirit of revelation, the spirit by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. It names a second gift, the gift of Aaron, which only God’s power can make work. It warns that without faith he can do nothing and should not ask for what he ought not. It invites him to ask to know mysteries and to translate sacred records.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 6–9 teaches that Heavenly Father speaks to us through the Holy Ghost. Why might verse 2 name both mind and heart, and how does verse 3 connect that to Moses?

contextNote.title: Where the answer arrives
contextNote.text: Oliver wanted to know how translation would work for him. Verse 2 says the Lord will speak “in your mind and in your heart” by the Holy Ghost. Verse 3 calls this “the spirit of revelation” and ties it to the spirit by which Moses brought Israel through the Red Sea. Verse 1 sets the conditions: asking in faith, with an honest heart. Verse 10 repeats that without faith he can do nothing. In this section, revelation is knowledge that reaches thought and feeling together.

passages.title: Revelation requires study before asking, not asking alone
passages.setting: Earlier in April 1829, revelations had promised Oliver Cowdery a gift to translate. He tried at Harmony, Pennsylvania, and did not succeed. This revelation, likely given in the second half of April, explained why. It told him to keep writing for Joseph Smith for now. It also promised he would help translate other records later.
passages.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery to keep writing for Joseph Smith until this record is finished. It promises other records he will later help translate. It says the privilege was taken away because he did not continue as he began. He had supposed it would be given when he only asked. He must study it out in his mind and then ask if it is right. If it is right, his bosom will burn; if not, he will have a stupor of thought. It says he feared, and the time for him to translate has passed. It ends by telling him to stand fast in the work he was called to do.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 6–9 uses verses 7–9 to teach how the Holy Ghost speaks. What does verse 8 ask Oliver to do before he asks, and how could you do that with a decision you face now?

contextNote.title: Study first, then ask
contextNote.text: Oliver’s attempt to translate failed, and verse 7 names the reason. He had taken “no thought save it was to ask” the Lord. Verse 8 gives the missing step: “study it out in your mind” first. Only then does he ask whether it is right. The answer comes as a burning in the bosom, or as a “stupor of thought” in verse 9. Verse 11 adds a second cause, saying simply that “you feared” when the time came. In this section, asking is the last step of a process that starts with effort.

passages.title: God foils a plot over the lost pages with a fuller record
passages.setting: In 1828 Martin Harris lost the first 116 pages of the Book of Mormon translation, which Joseph Smith called the Book of Lehi. By spring 1829 Joseph was translating again at Harmony, Pennsylvania, with Oliver Cowdery as scribe. Nearing the end, they weighed whether to retranslate the lost portion. This revelation told Joseph not to. The date is uncertain: the official heading says most likely April 1829, with parts possibly from summer 1828. The Joseph Smith Papers editors suggest part may have come in 1828 but was written down in 1829.
passages.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he lost the writings and his gift by giving them to a wicked man. His gift is now restored, and he is told to pray always and not run faster than his strength allows. It says wicked men have altered the stolen words. Their plan is to wait for a retranslation, then claim the two versions disagree. So Joseph must not translate those words again. Instead he is to translate the fuller account on the plates of Nephi, which covers the same period. The ancient prophets prayed that this gospel would reach the Lamanites and all people in the land. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice defines his church as whoever repents and comes to him.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 10–11 teaches that the Lord’s wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil. Read verses 38–45 with Words of Mormon 1:3–7: how was the remedy prepared long before the loss?

contextNote.title: Why Joseph would not retranslate
contextNote.text: The revelation describes a trap built around the lost pages. Verses 17–18 lay out the plan: hold altered copies, then claim a new translation contradicts them. Verse 30 forbids Joseph to translate those words again. Verses 38–41 point instead to a fuller account “engraven upon the plates of Nephi” covering the same period. Verse 43 explains the change: God’s “wisdom is greater than the cunning of the devil” and will protect the work. Here wisdom means a second record, already prepared, that makes the plot useless.

passages.title: Hyrum must obtain the word before he declares it
passages.setting: Hyrum Smith, Joseph Smith’s older brother, came to Harmony, Pennsylvania, in May 1829 to learn about the work. Joseph inquired through the Urim and Thummim and received this revelation for him. Joseph’s history places it after the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood, which he dated to 15 May 1829. Joseph Smith Papers notes suggest it came after Samuel Smith’s baptism, perhaps on 25 May. The pages of Revelation Book 1 that held it are missing.
passages.summary: The revelation opens with the same call to the harvest given to Oliver Cowdery in section 6. It tells Hyrum to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It says he will have a gift if he asks in faith with an honest heart. It tells him to trust the Spirit that leads to do good, do justly, walk humbly, and judge righteously. That Spirit will enlighten his mind and fill his soul with joy. He is not to preach until he is called. First he must obtain the word, studying what has gone forth and what is now being translated. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice promises power to become sons of God to all who receive him.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 10–11 teaches that as we seek to obtain God’s word, we receive his Spirit and power. According to verse 22, which two bodies of the Lord’s word was Hyrum told to study?

contextNote.title: Why Hyrum had to wait
contextNote.text: Verse 15 suggests Hyrum was ready to preach, and it tells him not to suppose he is called yet. Verse 21 gives the order: “first seek to obtain my word,” and only then declare it. Then his tongue will be loosed, and he will have the Spirit and power to convince. Verse 22 explains what obtaining means: studying the word already given and the record “now translating” at Harmony. Verse 26 asks him to treasure these things until the time comes. In this section, obtaining the word is study that comes before preaching.

passages.title: Anyone willing to reap is called, if humble and loving
passages.setting: Joseph Knight Sr. was a farmer and miller from Colesville, New York. He had helped Joseph Smith with food, money, and paper since 1827. In May 1829 Joseph and Oliver Cowdery ran short of supplies at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Knight soon came to Harmony with paper and enough food to finish the translation. Joseph’s history says Knight was anxious to know his duty, so Joseph asked the Lord for him. The exact day of Knight’s arrival is not recorded.
passages.summary: The revelation opens by announcing that a great and marvelous work is about to come forth. The voice speaks as God and calls its word sharper than a two-edged sword. It says the field is ready for harvest, and whoever reaps with might is called of God. It promises that those who ask will receive. Because Knight has asked, it tells him to keep the commandments and help establish the cause of Zion. It then says no one can assist unless humble, loving, faithful, hopeful, charitable, and temperate. It closes with the speaker naming himself the light and life of the world.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 teaches that each person can take part in God’s “great and marvelous work.” Verse 8 lists the qualities required to assist; which one did Knight show by bringing supplies, and which one could you work on?

contextNote.title: Who may help with the work
contextNote.text: Knight was not a scribe or a translator, so his place in the work was unclear. Verse 8 answers by naming the qualities a helper needs, not a skill or an office. Humility and love come first, then faith, hope, and charity. The list ends with temperance in “all things” entrusted to the helper’s care. Verse 6 had already given Knight a task: help bring forth the cause of Zion. Read together, the two verses say the task is open, but the character is required. In this passage, to “assist” means to support the work with a disciplined and loving life.

passages.title: An angel restores the authority to baptize
passages.setting: Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Joseph’s later history says the text raised a question about baptism for the remission of sins. On 15 May 1829 the two men went into the woods near the Susquehanna River to pray about it. They reported that an angel who called himself John, the Baptist of the New Testament, ordained them. This section is the ordination wording as recorded in Joseph’s history, written years later.
passages.summary: These are the words of an ordination, not a full revelation. The speaker calls Joseph and Oliver his “fellow servants.” He confers the Priesthood of Aaron in the name of Messiah. He says this priesthood holds the keys of the ministering of angels. It also holds the keys of the gospel of repentance and of baptism by immersion for remission of sins. He says it will not be taken from the earth until the sons of Levi again offer an offering in righteousness.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 and Joseph Smith—History 1:66–75 presents this ordination as the restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood. Verse 1 lists three keys; how does each one connect to what Joseph and Oliver were seeking that day?

contextNote.title: Authority tied to a specific task
contextNote.text: Joseph and Oliver had read about baptism for the remission of sins and wanted to know more. Verse 1 answers with authority rather than with instructions. It names three things this priesthood holds keys to: angels’ ministering, the gospel of repentance, and baptism by immersion. The last of these matches their question about baptism for remission of sins. The verse also looks forward, saying the authority will remain until the sons of Levi offer again. That phrase echoes Malachi 3:3, which Moroni had also quoted. Here “keys” means the right to perform and direct these specific acts.

passages.title: Eternal life is God’s greatest gift to those who endure
passages.setting: In late May or early June 1829, David Whitmer drove his wagon to Harmony, Pennsylvania. He moved Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to his father Peter Whitmer Sr.’s farm in Fayette, New York. There Joseph worked to finish translating the Book of Mormon. David and his brothers John and Peter Jr. became eager helpers and wanted to know their duties. Joseph’s history says he asked the Lord through the Urim and Thummim, and this revelation for David came first. Its wording suggests David had already been baptized that month.
passages.summary: The revelation opens with the same words given to Joseph Knight and others: a marvelous work is about to come forth. It says the field is ready to harvest and whoever reaps is called. It tells David to seek to establish Zion and keep the commandments in all things. If he endures to the end, he will have eternal life, the greatest gift of God. If he asks the Father in faith, he will receive the Holy Ghost. The Spirit will help him witness what he hears and sees and declare repentance. The speaker names himself Jesus Christ and says the gospel must go from the Gentiles to Israel. It ends by telling David he is called to assist and will be blessed if faithful.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 shows the Lord answering people who sincerely ask about their part. Verse 8 says David would “stand as a witness” of what he would “hear and see”; how did that promise come true in section 17?

contextNote.title: The greatest gift comes at the end
contextNote.text: David wanted to know what his part in the work should be. Verse 7 sets the long goal before the near task. Keeping the commandments and enduring to the end lead to eternal life. The verse ranks that gift “the greatest of all the gifts of God,” above every other. Verse 8 then names a nearer gift, the Holy Ghost, given so David can “stand as a witness” and declare repentance. The order matters: the Spirit equips the witness now, and endurance brings the final gift. In this passage, to “endure” means keeping commandments over a whole life, not for a season.

passages.title: The thing of most worth is bringing souls to Christ
passages.setting: John Whitmer was 26 and living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. Joseph Smith was there in June 1829 finishing the Book of Mormon translation. John sometimes wrote as scribe when Oliver Cowdery was away. He was probably baptized that month, and he asked Joseph to inquire about his duty. This revelation answered him, and an identical one went to his brother Peter Jr.
passages.summary: The revelation addresses John by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power. It says it will tell John something only he and the Lord know. John has many times wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It then answers: the thing of most worth is to declare repentance. By doing so he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 notes that John and Peter Whitmer Jr. received the same answer to a sincere personal question. Verse 4 says John had asked “many times”; what does verse 6 suggest you might ask the Lord about your own priorities?

contextNote.title: A private question, a plain answer
contextNote.text: Verse 4 reveals John’s private question: what would be “of the most worth” to him? Verse 3 frames the answer as personal, something known only to John and the Lord. Verse 6 then answers in one line: declare repentance and bring souls to Christ. The reward named is not wealth or status but rest with those souls. So the worth John sought is measured in people, not in his own gain. In this passage, “worth” means what lasts into the Father’s kingdom.

passages.title: The same personal answer comes to a second brother
passages.setting: Peter Whitmer Jr. was a 19-year-old tailor living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. He was baptized in Seneca Lake in June 1829. Like his brothers David and John, he wanted to know his duty in the work. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for him in early June. It matches word for word the one given to John, which seems to have come first.
passages.summary: The revelation addresses Peter by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power, and his arm is over all the earth. It promises to tell Peter something only he and the Lord know. Peter has often wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It answers that declaring repentance is of most worth. By that work he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 treats the twin Whitmer revelations as a pattern for personal direction. Compare verse 4 with verse 6: how did the answer to Peter’s private question give him a public task?

contextNote.title: Why repeat the same words
contextNote.text: Peter received the same text as his brother John, which raises a question. Verse 3 still says only Peter and the Lord know it. The answer lies in verse 4: the private part was Peter’s own repeated question. Two brothers had asked the same thing in secret, and verse 6 gives each the same answer. The repetition shows that the priority did not change from one person to the next. In this passage, the answer is shared, but the question being answered is personal.

passages.title: Three witnesses will see the plates by faith
passages.setting: Joseph Smith finished translating the Book of Mormon at Fayette, New York, in June 1829. The translation said three witnesses would see the plates and testify of them. Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and Martin Harris each wanted to be one of them. Joseph inquired through the Urim and Thummim, and this revelation was the answer. Joseph later said that not many days after, the four men went into the woods to pray for the promised view. The earliest surviving copy dates from no earlier than late 1834 and may have been edited.
passages.summary: The revelation tells the three men to rely on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. If they do, they will see the plates, breastplate, sword of Laban, Urim and Thummim, and Lehi’s directors. It says they will see these things by faith, like the prophets of old. Afterward they must testify of them by the power of God. Their testimony will help keep Joseph Smith from being destroyed. They will testify that they have seen as Joseph has seen. The voice declares that the translated book is true. If they obey, the gates of hell will not prevail against them.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 connects this revelation to the Testimony of Three Witnesses printed in the Book of Mormon. Verses 2 and 5 both tie the witnesses’ sight to faith; why might the Lord have required faith before giving physical evidence?

contextNote.title: Seeing is tied to testifying
contextNote.text: Joseph had seen the plates alone, which left him exposed to doubt and attack. Verse 3 states the purpose of the view: after seeing, the three must testify by God’s power. Verse 4 gives the reason, that Joseph “may not be destroyed,” so God’s purposes go forward. Verse 1 had set the condition, relying on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. So the sight was not a reward for curiosity but a burden of witness. In this passage, to “testify” means to share responsibility for the claim Joseph had carried alone.

passages.title: Building the Church begins with the worth of souls
passages.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in the first part of June 1829. It came after David Whitmer’s baptism and before a 14 June letter from Oliver Cowdery. It answers something Oliver wanted to know and speaks to him and David Whitmer. Joseph later said it made known the calling of twelve apostles and how to build up the Church. Later that month Oliver drafted “Articles of the Church of Christ,” drawn largely from the Book of Mormon.
passages.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery that what he has written is true and commands him to rely on it. It says the written record holds the foundation of the Church and gospel. It confirms Oliver’s baptism by Joseph Smith and says Joseph is called for the Lord’s purpose. It calls Oliver and David Whitmer to cry repentance, with the same calling as Paul. It explains that the worth of souls is great because the Redeemer suffered for all. It describes the joy of bringing even one soul to Christ. It then speaks of twelve disciples who will take Christ’s name, preach, and baptize. Oliver and David are told to search out the Twelve by their desires and works.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 18, “The Worth of Souls Is Great,” teaches that every person matters to God. Verses 10–16 move from Christ’s suffering to the preacher’s joy; whose soul could you help this week, and how?

contextNote.title: Why one soul matters so much
contextNote.text: Oliver and David were being called to preach before any church yet existed. Verse 10 says “the worth of souls is great” in the sight of God. Verses 11–12 explain that worth by the Redeemer’s suffering for all people and his rising again. Verse 13 adds that he has great joy in each person who repents. Verses 15–16 then turn that joy into a measure for the preachers’ own lives. A whole lifetime would be worth it for even one soul. In this passage, a soul’s “worth” is set by what Christ paid for it.

passages.title: Christ suffered so the repentant need not suffer
passages.setting: Martin Harris was a prosperous farmer near Palmyra, New York. He had agreed to pay the Palmyra printer Egbert Grandin to print the Book of Mormon. Grandin’s price for five thousand copies was $3,000, nearly all of Harris’s property. This revelation, given through Joseph Smith at Manchester, urged Harris to pay. On 25 August 1829 Harris mortgaged his farm to Grandin. Early printings dated the revelation March 1830, but historians now favor summer 1829.
passages.summary: The revelation opens with the speaker naming himself Alpha and Omega, Christ the Lord. It says every person must repent or suffer. It explains that “endless” and “eternal” punishment mean God’s punishment, because Endless is his name. It commands Martin Harris to repent, describing Christ’s own suffering that made him bleed at every pore. It tells Harris to preach only repentance for now. It commands him not to covet his property but to pay for printing the Book of Mormon. It tells him to pray aloud as well as in secret and to declare glad tidings. It ends by telling him to pay the printer, release himself from bondage, and come to Christ.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 19, “Learn of Me,” focuses on the Savior’s suffering and the peace He offers through repentance. Verse 23 invites Harris to “learn of me” and find peace; what do verses 16–19 teach you about why repentance brings peace?

contextNote.title: Suffering that was meant to be spared
contextNote.text: Harris was asked to risk his farm, and the revelation answers with a lesson about suffering. Verse 16 says God has “suffered these things for all” so they need not suffer if they repent. Verse 17 states the other side: those who do not repent must suffer as he did. Verse 18 then describes that suffering as pain that made him tremble and bleed at every pore. Verse 19 says he finished it anyway. Set against verse 26, Harris’s loss of property looks small. In this passage, Christ’s suffering is offered as a substitute that repentance accepts.

passages.title: A new church sets out its beliefs, offices, and ordinances
passages.setting: This document was known in Joseph Smith’s day as the Articles and Covenants. Joseph may have begun it in summer 1829, near the time Oliver Cowdery drafted his own articles. The earliest copies already describe the Church as organized on 6 April 1830, so parts were written or revised afterward. It was likely composed at or near Fayette, New York. At the first Church conference on 9 June 1830, Joseph read it and members approved it unanimously.
passages.summary: The document opens by dating the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It names Joseph Smith as first elder and Oliver Cowdery as second elder. It recounts Joseph’s forgiveness, his return to worldly vanities, an angel’s visit, and the translation of the Book of Mormon. It then states core beliefs about God, the Fall, Christ’s atonement, justification, and sanctification. It sets the requirements for baptism. It lists the duties of apostles and elders, priests, teachers, and deacons. It gives the exact words for baptism and for blessing the bread and wine. It closes with rules for conferences, records, licenses, and members who move.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 20–22, “The Rise of the Church of Christ,” highlights baptism and the sacrament as covenants. Compare the baptism requirements in verse 37 with the sacrament prayers in verses 77 and 79; which promises appear in both?

contextNote.title: Proof of change before baptism
contextNote.text: A new church had to decide who could join, and verse 37 gives the rule. Applicants must humble themselves, come with broken hearts, and witness before the church that they have repented. They must also be willing to take Christ’s name and serve him to the end. The final test is that they “truly manifest by their works” the Spirit of Christ. Verse 69 applies the same standard after baptism, asking for “a godly walk and conversation” before the church. JSP notes that Oliver Cowdery questioned part of this wording in summer 1830, and Joseph defended it. In this passage, readiness for baptism is shown by changed conduct, not only by belief.

passages.title: The new church must receive the prophet’s word as the Lord’s
passages.setting: On 6 April 1830 Joseph Smith and others met at Peter Whitmer Sr.’s home in Fayette, New York, to organize the Church. The group voted unanimously to accept Joseph and Oliver Cowdery as their teachers. Joseph ordained Oliver an elder, and Oliver ordained Joseph. They took bread and wine and laid hands on those present to confirm them. While the group was still together, Joseph dictated this revelation. Some early sources placed the event in Manchester, but the earliest manuscript and eyewitnesses support Fayette.
passages.summary: The revelation commands that a record be kept. In it Joseph Smith is to be called a seer, translator, prophet, apostle, and elder. It dates the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It tells the Church to heed Joseph’s words as if from the Lord’s own mouth, in patience and faith. If they do, the gates of hell will not prevail against them. It says the Lord has seen Joseph’s weeping for Zion and has forgiven him. It directs Oliver Cowdery to ordain Joseph. It calls Oliver an elder under Joseph’s hand and the Church’s first preacher.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 20–22, “The Rise of the Church of Christ,” teaches about following the Lord’s prophet. Verse 5 asks for “patience and faith”; why might patience be needed to receive a prophet’s counsel, and what does verse 6 promise?

contextNote.title: How to hear a prophet’s words
contextNote.text: The new members had to know how to treat Joseph’s revelations within the Church. Verse 4 tells them to heed “all his words and commandments” as he receives them. Verse 5 says to receive his word “as if from mine own mouth,” that is, as the Lord’s. The same verse adds the manner: “in all patience and faith,” not in haste. Verse 6 states the result, that the gates of hell will not prevail against them. In this passage, receiving the prophet’s word means accepting it with patience over time, not only with quick assent.

passages.title: Earlier baptisms cannot replace the new covenant
passages.setting: Ten days after the Church was organized, some believers wanted to join without being baptized again. Orson Pratt later described them as moral Baptists who accepted the Book of Mormon. Joseph Smith asked the Lord and dictated this revelation on 16 April 1830. The official heading places it at Manchester, New York, while the Joseph Smith Papers place it in Fayette Township. Early copyists often attached it to the Articles and Covenants as part of the baptism rules.
passages.summary: The revelation says all old covenants have been done away in this thing. It calls baptism into the Church a new and everlasting covenant that was from the beginning. It says a person baptized a hundred times gains nothing by it. No one can enter the strait gate by the law of Moses or by dead works. It says these dead works are why the Lord has built up this last covenant and church. It ends by telling them to enter at the gate as commanded and not to counsel God.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 20–22, “The Rise of the Church of Christ,” teaches that baptism is a covenant requiring proper authority. Verse 4 says “seek not to counsel your God”; how were the believers in verse 2 trying to counsel God?

contextNote.title: Why a sincere baptism was not enough
contextNote.text: These believers had already been baptized and saw no need to repeat it. Verse 2 answers that even a hundred baptisms avail “nothing” if they are dead works. Verse 3 explains the word: dead works are the reason a new covenant and church were needed. Verse 1 says the covenant is new, yet it was “from the beginning” as well. So the issue was not the person’s sincerity but the covenant and authority behind the act. In this passage, “dead works” means rituals done outside the covenant God has just restored.

passages.title: Five early believers each receive a distinct duty
passages.setting: Soon after the Church was organized on 6 April 1830, five men asked Joseph Smith to learn their duties. They were Oliver Cowdery, Hyrum Smith, Samuel H. Smith, Joseph Smith Sr., and Joseph Knight Sr. Joseph dictated five short revelations, apparently one after another. The official heading places them at Manchester, New York. The Joseph Smith Papers place the related meetings in Fayette Township and suggest they came before an 11 April meeting.
passages.summary: These are five brief revelations gathered into one section. Oliver Cowdery is told he is under no condemnation but must beware of pride. He is to make his calling known to the Church and the world. Hyrum Smith is also under no condemnation and is called to exhort and strengthen the Church. His duty is to the Church forever, because of his family. Samuel H. Smith is called to exhort and strengthen the Church but not yet to preach to the world. Joseph Smith Sr. is called to exhort and strengthen the Church from then on. Joseph Knight Sr. is told to take up his cross and pray aloud in every setting. He is also told it is his duty to unite with the true church.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 23–26, “Seek for the Things of a Better World,” shows the Lord giving individual direction. Each man in verses 1–7 gets a slightly different calling. What does Samuel’s “not as yet” in verse 4 teach about personal timing?

contextNote.title: A cross for the one not yet joined
contextNote.text: Four of the five men are told they are “under no condemnation,” but Joseph Knight Sr. is not. Verse 6 tells him instead to “take up your cross.” The cross is specific: praying aloud before the world, in his family, and among friends. Verse 7 adds that his duty is to unite with the true church. Knight had supported Joseph for years without joining, so open prayer and membership were public steps. In this passage, the “cross” is the cost of making private belief visible.

passages.title: Joseph’s strength lies in his calling, and the church must support it
passages.setting: This revelation came to Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. The church was less than four months old. In late June and early July, Joseph was arrested twice near Colesville, New York, and released both times. When he and Oliver went back to confirm new converts, a mob drove them away. The revelation was one of three given in this tense period, and its exact day is not recorded.
passages.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he was called to write the Book of Mormon and has been delivered from his enemies. It says he is not excused for his sins, but he should go and sin no more. After he sows and secures his fields, he is to visit the branches at Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester. If they receive him they will be blessed; if not, they will be cursed. His work is to pray, write what the Comforter gives, and expound the scriptures. Verse 9 says he will not have strength in temporal labors, because that is not his calling. Oliver is to keep declaring the gospel to the church and the world. Both men are to work miracles only when asked, take no purse or scrip, and let the church supply their needs.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 23–26 cites verses 1 and 8: the Savior can lift us “up out of” our afflictions. Verse 8 pairs “thou shalt have many” afflictions with “I am with thee”; how does verse 1 help explain why Joseph could trust that promise?

contextNote.title: Strength found in the calling itself
contextNote.text: Joseph had a farm at Harmony and a young church spread across three New York towns. Verse 9 settles which work comes first. It says he will not have strength in temporal labors, “for this is not thy calling.” Verse 3 still lets him sow and secure his fields before he travels. It then makes the branches responsible for supporting him. Verse 18 repeats the pattern: the church will give him food, clothing, and money “in the very hour.” Here “magnify thine office” means giving his main strength to expounding scripture and confirming the churches.

passages.title: Emma Smith is called as an elect lady with her own work
passages.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for his wife, Emma Hale Smith, at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. Emma had been baptized at Colesville, New York, on 28 June, but opposition delayed her confirmation. The earliest manuscript gives only the year, and the July date first appears in the 1833 Book of Commandments. It was the first known revelation of Joseph’s addressed to a woman. In 1835 Emma and William W. Phelps compiled the church’s first hymnal.
passages.summary: The revelation speaks to Emma Smith as a daughter in the Lord’s kingdom. It promises to preserve her life and give her an inheritance in Zion if she is faithful. It forgives her sins and calls her “an elect lady.” It tells her not to murmur over things she has not been shown. Her calling is to comfort Joseph, serve as his scribe, and be ordained to expound scripture and exhort the church. She is to lay aside the things of this world and make a selection of sacred hymns. The text warns against pride and promises a crown of righteousness if she keeps the commandments. It closes by saying this is the Lord’s voice to all.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Seek for the Things of a Better World” takes its title from verse 10 of this revelation to Emma. Verse 12 calls “the song of the righteous” a prayer; which hymn has felt like a prayer to you, and what blessing followed?

contextNote.title: Why a hymnbook belongs in a revelation
contextNote.text: Verse 11 gives Emma an unusual task: to select sacred hymns for the church. Verse 12 gives the reason for it. The Lord’s soul “delighteth in the song of the heart.” The verse then treats such singing as a kind of prayer. Because it is prayer, it can be answered “with a blessing upon their heads.” Verse 13 carries the thought forward by telling Emma to “lift up thy heart and rejoice.” In this passage a hymn is worship that God hears and answers, not only music for a meeting.

passages.title: Church decisions are to be made by common consent
passages.setting: This short revelation came at Harmony, Pennsylvania, in July 1830. It was addressed to Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, and John Whitmer. It came shortly after section 24, which told Joseph to tend his fields and then visit the branches. Joseph’s church work had left him little time for his farm. The Joseph Smith Papers editors supply the month, and no exact day is recorded.
passages.summary: The revelation tells the three men how to spend their time until the next conference. They are to study the scriptures and preach. They are to confirm the church at Colesville. They are also to do the work needed on the land. After they go west to hold the conference, further direction will be given. Verse 2 then states a general rule: all things in the church are to be done by common consent, with much prayer and faith.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Seek for the Things of a Better World” includes this revelation’s rule of common consent. Verse 2 joins consent to “much prayer and faith”; how might prayer change the way you sustain a decision in your ward or branch?

contextNote.title: Agreement as the church’s working rule
contextNote.text: The church was only months old, and its ways of making decisions were still taking shape. Verse 2 supplies one: “all things shall be done by common consent.” The verse ties that consent to “much prayer and faith,” not to a bare vote. Verse 1 shows the same patience on a small scale. Even the men’s next assignments will be “made known” only after the coming conference. In this passage common consent means members agreeing together, in faith, to what the church does.

passages.title: The sacrament’s meaning matters more than what is on the table
passages.setting: In August 1830, Newel and Sally Knight visited Joseph and Emma Smith at Harmony, Pennsylvania. Emma and Sally had not yet been confirmed, and the group planned to confirm them and take the sacrament. Joseph reported that a heavenly messenger met him as he went to buy wine. He wrote the first paragraph then; his later history says the rest was written in September. The longer text was first printed in the 1835 Doctrine and Covenants.
passages.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ. It says that what the Saints eat or drink in the sacrament does not matter if they remember his body and blood. It forbids buying wine or strong drink from enemies and allows only wine made new among themselves. It promises that Christ will drink of the fruit of the vine with his servants on the earth. It names those who will join him: Moroni, Elias, John the Baptist, Elijah, the patriarchs, Michael or Adam, and Peter, James, and John. It says John ordained Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to the first priesthood. It says Peter, James, and John ordained them apostles and gave them keys. It ends by telling them to put on “my whole armor” and stand.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “All Things Must Be Done in Order” uses this revelation to focus the sacrament on remembering Christ. The Church now uses water, as verse 2 allows; what in verse 2 will you deliberately remember at the sacrament this week?

contextNote.title: Remembrance, not the cup, is the point
contextNote.text: Joseph reported that this revelation came as he went to buy wine. Verse 2 says “it mattereth not” what is eaten or drunk in the sacrament. What matters is doing it “with an eye single to my glory.” The verse then names what is to be remembered: a body laid down and blood shed for sins. Verses 3–4 add a practical rule against buying wine from enemies. In this passage the sacrament is defined by remembrance, and the emblems serve that remembrance.

passages.title: Only Joseph receives revelations that command the church
passages.setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, shortly before the conference of 26 September. Joseph and Emma Smith had just moved there from Harmony, Pennsylvania. Hiram Page claimed to receive revelations through a stone about Zion and church order. Many members, including Oliver Cowdery and the Whitmer family, accepted them. Earlier that summer Oliver had written commanding Joseph to erase words from the church’s Articles and Covenants. Joseph sought guidance and dictated this revelation for Oliver.
passages.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery the church will hear him when he teaches by the Comforter. It then says only Joseph Smith is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church, “even as Moses.” Oliver is to be like Aaron, declaring what Joseph receives. He may speak by the Spirit, but he must not write by way of commandment or command Joseph. Oliver is sent to preach to the Lamanites and establish the church among them. The city of Zion’s location is not yet revealed, but it will be “on the borders by the Lamanites.” Oliver is to tell Hiram Page privately that his stone writings come from Satan. All things are to be done in order and by common consent.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “All Things Must Be Done in Order” draws its title from verse 13 of this revelation. How do verses 2 and 13 work together to protect a church from confusion like that caused by Hiram Page’s stone?

contextNote.title: One channel for the church’s commandments
contextNote.text: Hiram Page’s stone writings had won followers, and Oliver himself had tried to command Joseph. Verse 2 answers both problems at once. Only Joseph is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church. Verse 7 gives the reason: Joseph holds “the keys of the mysteries.” Verse 4 still lets Oliver speak and teach as the Comforter leads. Verse 5 limits his writing, which must be “by wisdom,” not by commandment. Verse 13 adds that all things must be done in order and by common consent. In this passage “appointed” means the one person authorized to give binding direction to the whole church.

passages.title: Christ will gather his elect, and Adam’s fall makes choice real
passages.setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, a few days before the 26 September conference. Six elders and three other members were present. Revelation Book 1 says they differed over Adam’s transgression and asked the Lord about it. Many members were also eager about the Book of Mormon’s promise of a gathering in America. Hiram Page’s competing revelations about Zion were circulating at the same time.
passages.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, who will gather his people “as a hen gathereth her chickens.” It forgives the elders and calls them to gather the elect to one place on this land. It describes Christ’s coming in glory, the Twelve judging Israel, and the rising of the righteous dead. Signs, plagues, and the fall of the great and abominable church come first. After the thousand years, a new heaven and earth replace the old. The text then says all of God’s commandments are spiritual, not temporal. It explains the devil’s rebellion, Adam’s fall, and the time of probation given for repentance. It says little children are redeemed through Christ and cannot sin until they become accountable.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Jesus Christ Will Gather His People” centers on this revelation’s promise of gathering. Verse 2 says Christ gathers those who hearken, humble themselves, and pray; which of those three most needs your attention now?

contextNote.title: Why temptation is allowed
contextNote.text: The elders had disagreed about Adam’s transgression. Verse 39 answers why the devil is allowed to tempt at all. Without temptation, people “could not be agents unto themselves.” The verse adds a plain image: without bitter, they “could not know the sweet.” Verse 40 then shows Adam tempted, yielding, and falling. Verse 42 holds back temporal death until angels can teach repentance and redemption. In this passage agency means a real choice, and the devil’s temptation supplies the other side of it.

passages.title: David Whitmer is rebuked while Peter and John are sent to preach
passages.setting: These three revelations came at Fayette, New York, in late September 1830. They followed the church’s second conference, which began on 26 September, before the elders dispersed. Each was addressed to one Whitmer brother: David, Peter Jr., and John. The conference had named David church record keeper, though his revelation does not mention it. The 1835 Doctrine and Covenants first combined the three texts into one section.
passages.summary: The revelation first rebukes David Whitmer for fearing man and thinking on earthly things. It says he has been persuaded by people the Lord did not command. He is to stay at his father’s house, ponder, and serve in the church nearby. Peter Whitmer Jr. is told to go with Oliver Cowdery on the mission to the Lamanites. He is to heed Oliver and pray for him in his afflictions. Only Joseph Smith is named as Oliver’s counselor in church matters. John Whitmer is told to begin preaching at once. His labor is to be at Philip Burroughs’ home and the region around it.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” covers these calls to the Whitmer brothers. Verse 1 rebukes fear of man, and verse 11 promises “I am with you”; where could that promise help you speak up about your faith?

contextNote.title: What went wrong with David
contextNote.text: Verse 1 names David’s first problem: he feared man and did not rely on the Lord. Verse 2 shows where his attention went instead, to “the things of the earth.” He had not heeded the Spirit or “those who were set over” him. He had been persuaded by people the Lord had not commanded. The Joseph Smith Papers editors say it is unclear whether this refers to his support of Hiram Page. Verse 3 states the result: he is “left to inquire” for himself. In this passage being persuaded means following voices outside the church’s order.

passages.title: Thomas Marsh is sent to preach while God cares for his family
passages.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for Thomas B. Marsh in September 1830. Joseph’s history ties it to the church conference at Fayette, New York, that began on 26 September. Marsh had first learned of the Book of Mormon in 1829, while it was being printed in Palmyra. He moved his family from Massachusetts to Palmyra in September 1830. Shortly before the conference, David Whitmer baptized him and Oliver Cowdery ordained him an elder.
passages.summary: The revelation blesses Thomas Marsh for his faith in the work. It recognizes his afflictions because of his family and promises they will one day believe and join him. It says the hour of his mission has come and his tongue will be loosed. He is to preach what was revealed to Joseph Smith and reap in a field “white already to be burned.” It says his sins are forgiven and his family shall live. He is to leave them only a little while, and the Lord will prepare a place for them. He will establish a church and be a physician to the church, but not to the world. He is told to be patient, govern his house in meekness, pray always, and be faithful to the end.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” includes this call to Thomas B. Marsh. Verse 9 says “revile not against those that revile” and “govern your house in meekness”; what would that look like at home this week?

contextNote.title: Leaving family for only a little time
contextNote.text: Marsh had just moved his wife and children to Palmyra when this call came. Verse 2 recognizes afflictions he has had “because of your family.” It also promises they will one day “be one with you” in the church. Verse 6 then sets the terms of his mission: he is to go “only for a little time.” The Lord adds, “I will prepare a place for them.” Verse 5 ties his labor to their welfare: “your family shall live.” In this passage the call limits his absence and promises his family’s care.

passages.title: New missionaries to the Lamanites must keep to written revelation
passages.setting: In September 1830, Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. were called to preach to the Lamanites, meaning American Indians in the West. Other elders wanted these peoples to hear the Book of Mormon too, so Joseph Smith asked whether more should go. This revelation answered at Manchester, New York, in October 1830, probably before 17 October. It named Parley P. Pratt, baptized only weeks earlier, and Ziba Peterson, an elder licensed in June 1830. The missionaries left in late October and reached the Missouri border early in 1831.
passages.summary: The revelation says Parley P. Pratt is to declare the gospel, learn of the Lord, and be meek and lowly of heart. He is to go with Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. into the wilderness among the Lamanites. Ziba Peterson is to go with them as well. The Lord says he will go with them and be their advocate with the Father. Nothing shall prevail against them. They are to heed what is written and claim no other revelation. They are to pray always that the written word will be opened to their understanding.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” includes this call to the mission among the Lamanites. Verse 1 asks Parley Pratt to “learn of me” as well as preach; how do verses 1 and 4 link learning and teaching?

contextNote.title: Bound to what is written
contextNote.text: The mission would take these men far from Joseph Smith, just after Hiram Page’s stone writings were rejected. Verse 4 sets their limits. They are to heed “that which is written” and “pretend to no other revelation.” The same verse tells them to pray for understanding of those writings. Verse 5 adds a warning to “trifle not.” Verse 3 explains why they could go without more instruction: the Lord promises to be in their midst. In this passage “pretend” means to claim, so the missionaries may not claim new revelation of their own.

passages.title: In the eleventh hour, new laborers are told to open their mouths
passages.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York, in early October 1830. It was for Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet, both baptized within the previous month. It called them to the ministry and told them how to preach. Thayre later recalled a vision that prepared him for it, though he told this decades afterward. Sweet soon left the church and helped form a small group called the Pure Church of Christ.
passages.summary: The revelation calls Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet to hear the Lord’s word, “sharper than a two-edged sword.” It sends them to declare the gospel to a crooked and perverse generation. It says the field is white for harvest and this is the eleventh hour. It describes the vineyard as corrupted, with many led astray by priestcrafts. The Lord says he has called this church out of the wilderness and will gather his elect. The men are told to open their mouths, and they will be filled. Their message is repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. They are to keep the church articles, use the Book of Mormon and the scriptures, and be ready for the Bridegroom.

lds.text: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” draws its title from verse 2 of this revelation. Verses 8–10 say “open your mouths” three times; what is one specific opening you could take this week to speak of Christ?

contextNote.title: A promise for new preachers
contextNote.text: Thayre and Sweet had been members for only weeks when this call came. Verse 8 answers how such new converts could preach: “Open your mouths and they shall be filled.” It compares them to Nephi, who journeyed from Jerusalem into the wilderness. Verse 10 repeats the promise and supplies the opening words: “Repent, repent.” Verse 3 explains the urgency, since it is “the eleventh hour.” In this passage being filled means receiving the words to say at the moment of speaking.

passages.title: A young convert is called to cry repentance before Christ comes
passages.setting: Orson Pratt was baptized by his older brother Parley on 19 September 1830, his nineteenth birthday. In October he traveled more than 200 miles to Fayette, New York, where Joseph Smith was staying. He asked Joseph to inquire of the Lord about his duty. Joseph dictated this revelation on 4 November 1830 in Orson’s presence, and John Whitmer wrote it down. Orson was ordained an elder about a month later and began preaching in Colesville.
passages.summary: The voice in the revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, the light of the world. It recalls that he gave his life so believers might become God’s sons. On that basis it calls Orson his son. Orson is blessed for believing and more blessed for being called to preach. He is told to cry repentance loudly to a “crooked and perverse generation.” The revelation describes signs before Christ’s coming: a darkened sun, a blood-red moon, and falling stars. It tells Orson to prophesy by the Holy Ghost and promises to be with him if he is faithful.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 calls readers to lift up their voices and witness of Jesus Christ. Verses 3–5 move from Christ’s sacrifice to Orson’s sonship to his call to preach; how does that order shape your view of service?

contextNote.title: Why Orson is called a son
contextNote.text: Orson Pratt was new to the faith and only nineteen. Verse 1 opens with “My son Orson,” and verse 3 explains the title. It says Christ gave his life so believers “might become the sons of God.” Verse 4 adds that Orson is blessed because he has believed. So sonship here rests on belief in Christ’s sacrifice, not on age or experience. Verse 5 then builds on that standing with a call to preach. In this passage, being a son is the ground from which the mission grows.

passages.title: A former preacher becomes Joseph Smith’s scribe and partner
passages.setting: Sidney Rigdon led a reformed Baptist congregation in northeastern Ohio. In November 1830 missionaries preached there, and Rigdon and many members joined the Church. In early December Rigdon and Edward Partridge traveled to New York to meet Joseph Smith. Joseph dictated this revelation on 7 December 1830 at or near Fayette. He had been revising the Bible since June 1830, and his earlier scribes had other duties.
passages.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, crucified so believers may become one with him as he is with the Father. It tells Sidney Rigdon that God has seen his works and prepared him for a greater work. It compares him to John, sent to prepare the way without knowing it. He had baptized without the Holy Ghost following; now those he baptizes will receive it by laying on of hands. The revelation promises miracles to believers and says the weak and unlearned will thresh the nations. It says the gospel came through Joseph, blessed in weakness, who holds keys while he abides in Christ. Sidney is to watch over Joseph, write for him, and not forsake him. If Sidney does not write, Joseph will prophesy and Sidney will preach and prove his words from the prophets.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 uses verses 13–15 and 24 to teach that members are called to witness of Jesus Christ. Verse 13 says the Lord calls “the weak things of the world”; how do verses 17–18 show the same pattern in Joseph’s calling?

contextNote.title: A scribe for the Bible revision
contextNote.text: Joseph’s scribes for his Bible revision, Oliver Cowdery and John Whitmer, had been given other duties. Verse 20 fills that gap: Sidney is commanded to “write for him.” The same verse says the scriptures will be given “even as they are in mine own bosom.” Verse 19 makes the job more than copying, since Sidney must watch over Joseph “that his faith fail not.” Verse 22 adds a personal bond: “tarry with him” and “forsake him not.” In this passage, writing for Joseph means being his steady partner in receiving scripture.

passages.title: Any man who embraces the call may be ordained to preach
passages.setting: Edward Partridge was a hatter from Painesville, Ohio, and a member of Sidney Rigdon’s congregation. His wife, Lydia, joined the Church after missionaries preached there in November 1830. Edward wanted to meet Joseph Smith first, so he came to New York with Rigdon and then asked for baptism. Joseph dictated this revelation for him on 9 December 1830 near Fayette. Joseph baptized him on 11 December, and Rigdon ordained him an elder on 15 December.
passages.summary: The voice speaks as the Lord God and tells Edward that his sins are forgiven. Edward is called to preach as with the voice of a trumpet. Sidney Rigdon is to lay hands on him so he receives the Holy Ghost. Edward is to cry, “Hosanna, blessed be the name of the most high God.” Then the revelation widens its call to all men. Anyone who comes to Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith embracing this call may be ordained and sent out. It closes with the voice, as Jesus Christ, saying he will suddenly come to his temple.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 teaches that the Lord prepares people for the work he wants them to do. What does verse 2 say the Holy Ghost will teach Edward Partridge, and why would a brand-new preacher need that?

contextNote.title: From one man’s call to every man’s
contextNote.text: The Church in late 1830 had few elders for a growing field. Verses 1–3 call one man, Edward Partridge, who had only just arrived. Verses 4–5 then extend “this calling and commandment” to all men who come forward. Verse 7 sets the one condition: they must embrace it “with singleness of heart.” Verse 8 gives the reason for haste, since the Lord says he will “suddenly come to my temple.” In this passage, singleness of heart means undivided commitment, and that is what qualifies a man to be sent.

passages.title: The first command to gather sends the Church to Ohio
passages.setting: In late December 1830 Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon were working on Joseph’s revision of the Bible. The Joseph Smith Papers place this revelation at Canandaigua, New York, about 30 December, soon after they arrived there. The official heading places it near Fayette in December 1830. Opposition to the Church was growing in New York, especially in Colesville. Oliver Cowdery was then leading the mission to the Lamanites, bound for western Missouri.
passages.summary: The revelation tells Joseph and Sidney to stop translating until they go to the Ohio. It gives two reasons: “because of the enemy” and “for your sakes.” First they must preach and strengthen the branches, especially in Colesville. It says the Colesville members pray in much faith. Then it commands the Church to assemble in the Ohio before Oliver Cowdery returns. It ends by telling every man to choose for himself.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 37–40 cites this section to teach that God gathers his people to bless them. Verse 2 says the Colesville Saints “pray unto me in much faith”; why might the Lord send leaders to strengthen them before the move?

contextNote.title: Gathering becomes a command with a place
contextNote.text: Earlier revelations had spoken of gathering, but none had told the Church where to move. Verse 3 names one: the Church should “assemble together at the Ohio.” Verse 1 gives the reason, “because of the enemy and for your sakes.” The Joseph Smith Papers tie this to rising opposition in New York. Verse 2 sets an order, though, since the branches must be strengthened before anyone leaves. Verse 4 then leaves the choice to each person. In this passage, to assemble means to move and settle together in one region.

passages.title: Be one, and go to Ohio to receive the law
passages.setting: The Church held its third conference at Fayette, New York, on 2 January 1831. Three days earlier a revelation had told members to gather in Ohio. Members at the conference wanted to know more, so Joseph Smith inquired before the congregation. Some were reluctant to move, and John Whitmer recorded that some suspected Joseph of inventing the command for gain. A Waterloo writer reported that property owners resisted at first but agreed after fasting and prayer.
passages.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, the Creator, who took the Zion of Enoch to himself. It warns that the wicked are kept in chains of darkness for judgment. It tells the Saints he is in their midst though unseen, and that some are clean but not all. It reveals that enemies in “secret chambers” plot their destruction. It promises a land of inheritance if they seek it with all their hearts. It commands each person to esteem his brother as himself and gives a parable of a father who favors one son. It then explains the move: in Ohio they will receive the law and be “endowed with power from on high.” Men chosen by the Church will care for the poor and property, and all are to warn neighbors meekly.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 37–40 uses verses 24–27 to teach that God wants his people to be one. Read the parable in verse 26 beside verses 34–35; what practical steps toward being one does this section require?

contextNote.title: Why the Saints must be one
contextNote.text: The New York members faced a costly move, and rich and poor stood to lose different things. Verse 16 says “the poor have complained” and the Lord is “no respecter of persons.” Verses 24–25 repeat the command to esteem one’s brother as oneself. Verse 26 then pictures a father who dresses one son in robes and another in rags. Verse 27 draws the line: “if ye are not one ye are not mine.” Verses 34–35 turn that into practice, naming men to keep the poor from suffering. In this passage, being one means sharing the cost of gathering so no one is left in rags.

passages.title: A minister is offered deliverance if he will be baptized
passages.setting: On 5 January 1831, three days after the Church conference, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Fayette, New York. It was for a minister named James, who had covenanted to obey any command given through Joseph. Later printings name him James Covel or Covill. The Joseph Smith Papers favor James Covel, a Methodist elder near Canandaigua, but no source settles his identity.
passages.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, who gives power to become his sons to all who receive him. It defines the gospel as repentance, baptism by water, and then the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It tells James that his heart is right at this time. It also says he has rejected the Lord many times because of pride and worldly cares. If he will arise and be baptized, it promises a blessing greater than he has known. It calls him to preach, but in the Ohio, not in the eastern countries. It says the Ohio people pray in faith, and judgment will be stayed only if they repent. James is to baptize and lay on hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 37–40 points to James Covel’s story when teaching that eternal riches outweigh earthly ones. What does the phrase “at this time” in verse 8 suggest about why verse 10 urges him to act now?

contextNote.title: Why James had seen great sorrow
contextNote.text: James came with a sincere promise, yet the revelation looks back on a troubled past. Verse 8 says his heart is “right before me at this time.” Verse 9 explains his sorrow: he had rejected the Lord “many times because of pride and the cares of the world.” Verse 10 answers that pattern with an opening: “the days of thy deliverance are come.” The condition is plain, since he must arise and be baptized. In this passage, sorrow is the result of repeated refusal, and deliverance depends on acting now.

passages.title: Fear and worldly cares led a covenant maker to break his word
passages.setting: James Covel left Fayette within a day of the 5 January revelation, without explaining why. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon were left asking why he had not obeyed. Joseph later recalled that this revelation, dated 6 January 1831, gave the reason. His history says Covel returned to his former principles and people.
passages.summary: The revelation says James Covel’s heart had been right, for he covenanted to obey the Lord’s word. He received the word with gladness. It says Satan tempted him straightway. The fear of persecution and the cares of the world led him to reject the word. So he broke the covenant. The revelation leaves his outcome with the Lord, to do “as seemeth me good.”

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 37–40 uses James Covel’s experience to contrast earthly cares with the riches of eternity. Verse 2 says Satan tempted him “straightway” after he received the word with gladness; what might help a person hold on in that moment?

contextNote.title: How a glad start ended
contextNote.text: Joseph and Sidney wanted to know why a man who promised obedience had walked away. Verse 1 says that his heart had been right and his covenant real. Verse 2 gives the cause in two parts: “the fear of persecution and the cares of the world.” The wording recalls Jesus’s parable of the sower, where seed received with joy withers or is choked. Verse 3 states the result: he “broke my covenant.” In this passage, rejecting the word is the end of a slide that began with temptation right after gladness.

passages.title: Disciples are those who receive the law and do it
passages.setting: Joseph Smith arrived in Kirtland, Ohio, from New York on 4 February 1831 and dictated this revelation that day. Leman Copley, a recent convert, had offered Joseph and Sidney Rigdon houses and provisions on his farm in Thompson.
