They should list the names of those who oppressed them. A committee might take statements and affidavits and collect libelous publications. The goal is to publish the record and present it to the heads of government. The letter calls this an “imperative duty” to God, to families, to widows and orphans, and to the rising generation. Many people of all faiths, it says, miss the truth only because they do not know where to find it. It ends by urging the Saints to do all they can, then stand still and trust God.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 121–123 draws attention to the small helm in verse 16. What does verse 17 ask the Saints to do before they “stand still,” and what does it promise afterward?

contextNote.title: Truth hidden for want of a guide
contextNote.text: The Saints had been driven out, and verses 4–5 note that many published accounts were hostile. Verse 12 explains why gathering the facts matters beyond the Saints themselves. Many people in every church are “only kept from the truth” because they “know not where to find it.” Verse 13 draws the result: the Saints should wear out their lives bringing hidden things to light. Verse 16 adds that a very small helm can steer a large ship in a storm. In this passage, careful record-keeping is a way to make the truth findable for others.

passages.title: Nauvoo must build a temple where sacred ordinances belong
passages.setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Nauvoo, Illinois, on 19 January 1841. The Saints had been forced out of Missouri after Governor Lilburn Boggs’s order of 27 October 1838. They settled at Commerce, Illinois, renamed it Nauvoo, and made it Church headquarters. Joseph Smith Sr., David Patten, and Edward Partridge had died since 1838. Church clerk Robert Thompson copied the revelation into the Book of the Law of the Lord.
passages.summary: The revelation accepts Joseph’s offering and calls for a proclamation to the kings and rulers of the earth. It names helpers, including Robert Thompson and John Bennett, and praises Hyrum Smith and George Miller. It commands the Saints to bring their wealth and skill and build a temple in Nauvoo. Baptisms for the dead outside the temple are accepted only for a set time. If the Saints do not build, they will be rejected as a church with their dead. The Lord accepts the offering of those hindered in Jackson County and tells the Saints to build again. A boarding house called the Nauvoo House is to be funded by stock under set rules. The revelation then counsels many individuals, calls Hyrum as patriarch, adds William Law to the First Presidency, and names the Church’s quorum leaders.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 124, “A House unto My Name,” presents the temple as the place for sacred ordinances. According to verses 39–41, what were the Saints to receive in a house built to the Lord’s name?

contextNote.title: When enemies stop the work
contextNote.text: The Saints had been told to build a city and temple in Jackson County, but mobs drove them out in 1833. That left a question: had they failed a command? Verse 49 says that when people work with all their might and enemies hinder them, God no longer requires the work. Instead he accepts “their offerings.” Verse 51 applies this rule directly to Jackson County. Verse 55 then gives a new command to build in Nauvoo. In this passage, accepting an offering means the effort counts even when the result was blocked.

passages.title: Scattered Iowa Saints are told to gather and build Zarahemla
passages.setting: After leaving Missouri in 1839, most Latter-day Saints settled in Hancock County, Illinois. Smaller groups lived in scattered settlements across the river in Iowa Territory. In early March 1841, Joseph Smith dictated this answer at Nauvoo to a question about those Iowa Saints. It may relate to an 11 March visit by John Smith, who led the Iowa stake, to learn the Lord’s will. The exact day is uncertain because the first copy was made later without a date.
passages.summary: The section opens with a question about the Lord’s will for the Saints in Iowa Territory. The answer sets a condition: if they will do his will, they should gather. They are to gather to places the Lord appoints through Joseph Smith. They are to build cities so they will be ready for what is coming. The revelation names a city to be built across the river from Nauvoo, called Zarahemla. People arriving from every direction may settle there. They may also take inheritances in Nashville, in Nauvoo, or in the appointed stakes.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 includes this revelation but centers its study on sections 126–128. Why might verse 2 tie gathering to being “prepared for that which is in store,” and what does verse 4 add?

contextNote.title: Gathering instead of scattering
contextNote.text: The Iowa Saints were spread across small, isolated settlements. Verse 2 answers by telling them to gather to appointed places and build cities. The gathering is conditional: it applies to those who “will do my will.” Verse 3 then makes the order concrete by naming one city, Zarahemla, opposite Nauvoo. Verse 4 opens it to newcomers “from the east, and the west, and the north, and the south.” The stated purpose in verse 2 is to be “prepared for that which is in store.” In this passage, gathering means building together in named places, not settling alone.

passages.title: Brigham Young’s long missions end with a charge to his family
passages.setting: Brigham Young left Nauvoo in 1839 for a mission to England with other apostles. His wife, Mary Ann Angell Young, and their children faced poverty and illness while he was gone. Young, Heber Kimball, and John Taylor arrived back in Nauvoo on 1 July 1841. Eight days later, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Young’s home. Willard Richards copied it into the Book of the Law of the Lord that December.
passages.summary: This short revelation addresses Brigham Young as a dear and well-beloved brother. The Lord’s voice tells Brigham he no longer has to leave his family as before. It says his offering is accepted. It says the Lord has seen his labor and travel for His name. Then it gives two commands. Brigham is to send the Lord’s word abroad. He is also to take special care of his family from then on.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 draws from verse 3 that the Lord wants His disciples to care for their families. How does verse 2 describe Brigham’s past years of travel before verse 3 changes his duties?

contextNote.title: Sending the word without leaving home
contextNote.text: Brigham Young had spent much of the past decade away on missions. Verse 1 says that kind of leaving is “no more required.” The reason given is that his offering is already acceptable. Verse 2 adds that the Lord has seen his “labor and toil in journeyings.” Verse 3 then joins two duties in one command: he must “send my word abroad” and “take especial care of your family.” As President of the Twelve, he could send others out rather than go himself. In this passage, the release from travel is a new assignment, not a retirement.

passages.title: From hiding, Joseph orders witnessed records of baptisms for the dead
passages.setting: In August 1842 Joseph Smith faced arrest and possible extradition to Missouri. Former Missouri governor Lilburn Boggs and John Bennett had accused him of a part in an attempt on Boggs’s life. Joseph hid with friends in and near Nauvoo and across the river in Iowa Territory. On 1 September he dictated this letter to William Clayton. It was read to the Saints in the grove near the temple site on 4 September. Baptisms for the dead had been performed since 1840, and the temple font was dedicated in November 1841.
passages.summary: Joseph Smith writes to the Saints explaining why he has left home for a time. He says enemies in Missouri and Illinois pursue him without just cause. He has left his business with agents and will return when the storm passes. He says danger has been his lot all his life, yet God has always delivered him. A revelation then tells the Saints to continue the temple work with redoubled diligence. It directs that a recorder witness every baptism for the dead, so what is recorded on earth may be recorded in heaven. The records are to be kept in order in the temple. Joseph closes, unable to speak in person, and promises more letters.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 uses verses 2–4 to teach reliance on the Lord in hard times. What does Joseph call “a second nature” in verse 2, and how does verse 4 turn that into direction for the Saints?

contextNote.title: Why a witness must see and hear
contextNote.text: Baptisms for the dead had been performed for two years, with records that varied in detail. Verse 6 now asks for a recorder who sees and hears each baptism. Verse 7 gives the reason: so that “in all your recordings it may be recorded in heaven.” The same verse links the earthly record to binding on earth and in heaven. Verse 8 explains the timing: the Lord is “about to restore many things” about priesthood. Verse 9 adds that the records must be kept in order in the temple archives. In this passage, a careful record is part of the ordinance itself, not an afterthought.

passages.title: Records and ordinances weld the living and the dead together
passages.setting: A week after his first letter, Joseph Smith was still hiding from officers sent to arrest him. He dictated this second letter on 7 September 1842 at the Nauvoo home of Edward Hunter. Officers from Adams County and an agent from Missouri had come for him on 3 September. The letter was read to the Saints at the grove near the temple on 11 September. That evening the general church recorder began a new book following its instructions. It was printed in the Times and Seasons on 1 October 1842.
passages.summary: Joseph Smith resumes the subject of baptism for the dead in a second letter. He revises his earlier instruction so each ward may have its own recorder and witnesses. A general recorder will then copy these certified records into a church book. Citing Revelation 20 and Matthew 16, he says what is recorded on earth is recorded in heaven. He calls the baptismal font a likeness of the grave, placed beneath where the living meet. Quoting Paul and Malachi, he says the living and the dead cannot be made perfect without each other. He then recalls voices from heaven: Moroni at Cumorah, Michael, Peter, James, and John, and others. He calls for courage and asks the Saints to present “a book containing the records of our dead” in the temple.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 teaches from verses 15–18 that the salvation of ancestors is essential to our own. According to verse 18, what “welding link” is needed, and why does verse 24 ask for a book of records?

contextNote.title: The “welding link” between generations
contextNote.text: Verse 17 quotes Malachi: the earth will be cursed unless the hearts of fathers and children turn. Verse 18 asks what could link the generations and answers, “It is the baptism for the dead.” Verse 15 gives the reason: “they without us cannot be made perfect—neither can we without our dead.” Verse 18 then widens the idea into a “welding together of dispensations, and keys.” Verses 8–9 explain what makes such a link hold: priesthood authority and a faithful record. In this passage, the “welding link” is an ordinance, done and recorded, that joins the living and the dead.

passages.title: A handshake test tells true messengers from false ones
passages.setting: On 9 February 1843, several visitors called at Joseph Smith’s home in Nauvoo. Parley and Orson Pratt were among them; Parley had returned to the city two days before. Joseph talked with them informally about how to tell true heavenly messengers from false ones. He had taught similar ideas in 1839, while Parley was jailed in Missouri. William Clayton and Willard Richards both recorded the remarks. Orson Pratt adapted Clayton’s version for the 1876 Doctrine and Covenants.
passages.summary: These instructions say there are two kinds of beings in heaven. Angels are resurrected and have bodies of flesh and bones, as Jesus said of himself. The spirits of just men made perfect are not resurrected but share the same glory. When a messenger claims to come from God, ask him to shake hands. An angel will do so, and you will feel his hand. A just spirit will not move, because deceiving is against heaven’s order, but he will still give his message. If the devil comes as an angel of light, you will feel nothing and can detect him. The section calls these “three grand keys” for judging any messenger.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 129–132 includes this section in its week but focuses on sections 130 and 132. Why does verse 7 say a just spirit will not shake hands, and how does that make the test in verse 8 work?

contextNote.title: Detecting a counterfeit messenger
contextNote.text: Joseph Smith had taught about discerning messengers as early as 1839. Verse 8 gives the test for a deceiver: he offers his hand, but nothing is felt. The test works because verses 1–3 first define what real messengers are. An angel has a body and can be touched, as verse 5 says. A just spirit will not pretend to have one, because that is “contrary to the order of heaven” (verse 7). Only the deceiver tries to seem what he is not. In this passage, a “key” is a practical test that exposes a false appearance.

passages.title: Joseph teaches that God is embodied and knowledge survives death
passages.setting: On Sunday, 2 April 1843, Joseph Smith was in Ramus, also called Macedonia, Illinois. He had spent the night at the home of Benjamin and Melissa Johnson. Orson Hyde preached that morning, and Joseph later corrected parts of his sermon. Some followers of William Miller expected Christ to return the next day, and Joseph addressed that interest. William Clayton recorded the teachings, which were drawn out by questions from those present. Parts of Willard Richards’s version became section 130 in 1876.
passages.summary: In separate teachings, Joseph says the Savior will appear as “a man like ourselves.” He says the same “sociality” will continue there, joined with eternal glory. He calls the idea that the Father and Son dwell in a person’s heart false. He says angels who minister to this earth belong or have belonged to it, and God’s dwelling is “a great Urim and Thummim.” He repeats a prophecy from 25 December 1832 that bloodshed before Christ’s coming will begin in South Carolina, probably over “the slave question.” He recalls a voice saying he would see the Son of Man if he lived to eighty-five. Knowledge gained in this life rises in the resurrection, and every blessing comes by obeying a law. The Father and Son have bodies of flesh and bones, but the Holy Ghost is a personage of Spirit.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 129–132 uses verses 20–21 to teach that God blesses those who obey His laws. According to verses 18–19, what advantage carries into the world to come, and what does verse 19 say produces it?

contextNote.title: Blessings built on laws
contextNote.text: Verses 14–17 decline to fix a date for Christ’s coming. Verses 20–21 turn instead to how blessings come. Every blessing rests on a law “irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world.” A person obtains a blessing by obeying the law on which it is “predicated.” Verses 18–19 apply the same logic to learning, gained “through his diligence and obedience.” Both passages tie future reward to present conduct rather than to timing. In this passage, “predicated” means each blessing is built on its own specific law.

passages.title: The highest celestial degree requires the covenant of marriage
passages.setting: In mid-May 1843 Joseph Smith visited Ramus, also called Macedonia, Illinois. On 16 May he taught William Clayton and Benjamin and Melissa Johnson at the Johnson home. His subject was priesthood and the sealing of marriage. On 17 May he preached on 2 Peter 1 and spoke again that evening. Clayton recorded these teachings in his journal, and they were later combined as section 131.
passages.summary: The section opens with three heavens or degrees within the celestial glory. To obtain the highest, a man must enter an order of the priesthood. A bracketed note explains this as the new and everlasting covenant of marriage. Without it, he may enter another degree but cannot have an increase. A note dated 17 May defines the “more sure word of prophecy.” It means knowing by revelation that one is sealed up to eternal life. The section says no one can be saved in ignorance. It ends by saying all spirit is matter, too fine to be seen now.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 129–132 teaches that Heavenly Father made it possible for families to be eternal. How do verses 2–4 connect marriage with what this section calls “increase”?

contextNote.title: Marriage as an order of the priesthood
contextNote.text: Verse 1 divides the celestial glory into three degrees. Verse 2 then states what reaches the highest one. Its answer is “this order of the priesthood,” which the bracketed note calls the covenant of marriage. Verses 3–4 state the result of not entering it: “that is the end of his kingdom.” The missing blessing is named as “increase.” Verse 5 adds the idea of knowing that one is “sealed up unto eternal life.” In this passage, the order is a sealed marriage covenant tied to eternal increase.

passages.title: Sealed marriage endures beyond death, and plural marriage is justified by command
passages.setting: On 12 July 1843, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation to William Clayton in his Nauvoo office. The official heading says Joseph likely knew some of its principles well before 1843. Hyrum Smith urged him to write it down, hoping it would persuade Emma Smith to accept plural marriage. The Joseph Smith Papers editors count about twenty-five confidential plural sealings by then, many unknown to Emma. Emma rejected the document and later destroyed the original, but a copy by Joseph Kingsbury survived. It was first published in 1852 and added to the Doctrine and Covenants in 1876.
passages.summary: The revelation answers Joseph’s question about how God justified Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and Solomon in having many wives and concubines. It reveals a “new and everlasting covenant,” saying covenants not sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise end at death. Marriages made only for this world end then, but marriages sealed by the one holding the keys endure toward exaltation. It says Abraham did not sin in taking Hagar and concubines because God commanded it, and David sinned only concerning Uriah’s wife. It confirms Joseph’s power to seal on earth and in heaven. Emma Smith is told to receive Joseph’s wives and cleave to him or be destroyed; if she forgives him, she will be blessed. Under the “law of the priesthood,” a man may marry more virgins with his first wife’s consent. If she rejects the law, verse 64 says she will be destroyed, and verse 65 frees him from “the law of Sarah,” her consent.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 129–132 draws eternal families from verses 13–21 and calls plural marriage acceptable only when God commands it. How do verses 1–2 and 29–40 present the revelation as an answer to Joseph’s question about ancient prophets?

contextNote.title: What makes a covenant last
contextNote.text: Joseph asked about ancient plural marriages, but the revelation first sets a wider rule. Verse 7 says every covenant or contract ends at death unless it is sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise. It must also be made through the one person appointed to hold “this power,” named as Joseph. Verse 15 applies the rule to marriage: a covenant made “so long as he is in the world” ends with death. Verse 19 states the contrast, a sealed marriage “of full force when they are out of the world.” The later verses on plural marriage (verses 34–39 and 61–65) rest on this same claim of sealing authority. In this passage, “sealed” means authorized by God through a single key holder so that a bond outlasts death.

passages.title: Saints must leave Babylon and prepare to meet the Bridegroom
passages.setting: Church leaders held a conference at Hiram, Ohio, on 1–2 November 1831 to plan publishing Joseph Smith’s revelations. On 1 November Joseph dictated a revelation to serve as the book’s preface, now section 1. A later history says he dictated this one on 3 November, after elders asked about preaching and gathering. One early copy is dated 2 November, but the Joseph Smith Papers editors favor Whitmer’s 3 November copy. It came to be called the appendix. It was first printed in 1833, but not in the Book of Commandments, whose printing was stopped by violence in Missouri.
passages.summary: The Lord’s voice calls on the Church to hear, for he will suddenly come to his temple in judgment. It tells the Saints to prepare, sanctify themselves, and gather to Zion, leaving Babylon behind. Elders are to go to all nations, first the Gentiles and then the Jews. Gentiles are to flee to Zion and Judah to Jerusalem, but not in haste. The revelation describes the Lord’s coming: lands joined, those in the north countries returning, and the saints rising from their graves. It pictures Christ in red garments, having “trodden the wine-press alone,” while his redeemed speak of his loving kindness. The Lord sent the gospel in plainness so the weak could prepare, and these commandments now go to all. Those who will not hear face darkness, because they rejected his servants.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 133–134 reads verses 4–14 as Christ’s call to reject Babylon and come to Zion. In verses 5 and 14, what does leaving Babylon require, and how does verse 15 caution the Saints?

contextNote.title: Babylon as a condition, not a city
contextNote.text: According to a later history, elders asked how the Saints should gather and preach. Verse 14 defines what they are leaving: “spiritual Babylon.” It locates Babylon in “the midst of wickedness,” not on a map. Verse 5 pairs the departure with a demand: “Be ye clean.” Verse 15 sets the pace: “let not your flight be in haste,” with all things prepared first. Verse 19 gives the purpose of leaving: to go out and meet the Bridegroom. In this passage, going out of Babylon means separating from wickedness while preparing for Christ.

passages.title: Governments must protect conscience but never control it
passages.setting: A general assembly of Church members met in Kirtland, Ohio, on 17 August 1835 and accepted the first edition of the Doctrine and Covenants. Oliver Cowdery and William W. Phelps then presented this declaration, and the assembly voted to print it in the book. Joseph Smith was away in Michigan Territory, and the author is uncertain; Cowdery may have written most of it. The Saints’ 1833 expulsion from Jackson County, Missouri, was a main reason for it. The JSP links the last paragraph to Missouri charges that the Church favored abolition.
passages.summary: This is a declaration of belief, not a revelation; each paragraph begins “We believe.” It says God instituted governments and holds people accountable for how they make and run laws. Good laws must protect conscience, property, and life. People must sustain the governments that protect their rights, and sedition is condemned. Civil officers should punish crime but never control conscience, and no religion should be favored by the state. Churches may discipline members only by removing fellowship, never by taking property or life. People should appeal to the law for wrongs, but may defend themselves when the law cannot act in time. The last paragraph says preaching to enslaved people against their masters’ wishes is unlawful and dangerous.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 133–134 uses this declaration to teach that governments should protect the freedom to worship. How do verses 4 and 9 balance obeying the law with keeping religion free from state control?

contextNote.title: Freedom of conscience as the test of a government
contextNote.text: The Saints had just lost homes and land in Jackson County without protection from the state. Verse 4 answers a basic question: how far may government reach into religion? It says the magistrate “should restrain crime, but never control conscience.” Verse 2 gives the reason: no government keeps peace unless it secures “the free exercise of conscience.” Verse 9 adds the other side, rejecting any union of one church with civil power. In this passage, conscience means a person’s religious belief and worship, answerable to God alone.

passages.title: The deaths at Carthage are presented as a sealing witness
passages.setting: Joseph Smith and his brother Hyrum were shot by a mob at the jail in Carthage, Illinois, on 27 June 1844. John Taylor was wounded, and Willard Richards escaped unhurt. This statement was written soon after and placed at the end of the 1844 edition of the Doctrine and Covenants. That edition was nearly ready for printing in Nauvoo when the killings happened. The official heading names no author, but the statement is traditionally attributed to John Taylor.
passages.summary: This is not a revelation but a written announcement and tribute, speaking as “we.” It reports that Joseph and Hyrum Smith were shot at Carthage Jail by a mob of 150 to 200 men. It records their last words and says John Taylor was wounded and Willard Richards escaped. It then praises Joseph Smith’s work, including the Book of Mormon and the revelations in this book. It quotes Joseph saying he went “like a lamb to the slaughter” with a clear conscience. It adds that Hyrum read a passage from Ether 12 before leaving for Carthage. It gives the brothers’ ages and calls them martyrs. It ends by saying their innocent blood, on Carthage jail, Illinois, and the nation, is a witness to the gospel. That blood will cry to the Lord until he avenges it.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 135–136 presents Joseph and Hyrum Smith as faithful witnesses who sealed their testimony with their lives. What does verse 3 list as Joseph Smith’s work, and which part of that list matters most in your own faith?

contextNote.title: Why the statement calls their blood a seal
contextNote.text: Readers in 1844 had to make sense of a prophet killed in custody. Verse 3 frames the deaths as a seal: he “sealed his mission and his works with his own blood.” Verse 1 opens the same way, saying the announcement is made “to seal the testimony” of this book. Verse 5 supplies the legal image behind the word: “the testators are now dead, and their testament is in force.” Verse 7 then places that blood on Carthage jail, on Illinois for its broken pledge, and on the nation. In this passage, to seal means to confirm a testimony as final, the way a death puts a will into effect.

passages.title: The westward camp must move as a covenant people
passages.setting: The Saints had left Nauvoo in 1846 and wintered on the Missouri River. Brigham Young gave this revelation at Winter Quarters on 14 January 1847. The camp was near Council Bluffs, on Omaha land, and planning the spring trek west. The revelation set out how the companies would be organized and prepared.
passages.summary: The revelation calls itself “the Word and Will of the Lord” for the camp traveling west. It orders the people into companies with captains of hundreds, fifties, and tens, under the Twelve Apostles. Each company covenants to keep the commandments, gathers supplies, and cares for the poor and widows. Pioneers are to go ahead and plant crops for those who follow. It names Ezra T. Benson, Erastus Snow, Orson Pratt, Wilford Woodruff, Amasa Lyman, and George A. Smith to organize companies. Then it gives rules for daily conduct: keep pledges, stop quarreling, return what is borrowed, and praise the Lord. It says the people must be tried, and calls Joseph Smith’s death needed to seal his testimony.
passages.dateLabel: 14 January 1847 · Winter Quarters, unorganized territory, now Nebraska

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 135–136 treats this revelation as counsel for the Saints’ journey and for personal trials. Which of the rules in verses 20–29 would most help the people you travel through life with?

contextNote.title: Hardship as preparation for glory
contextNote.text: The camp had been driven out, and many wondered why. Verse 31 gives an answer: “My people must be tried in all things.” The purpose is stated in the same verse, to prepare them for “the glory of Zion.” Verse 37 adds that they are “not yet pure” and cannot yet bear that glory. That is why the practical rules in verses 20–27 matter: honesty and peace are part of the preparation. In this passage, being tried means a testing that shapes a people for what is promised.

passages.title: God judges the dead by the desires of their hearts
passages.setting: On the evening of 21 January 1836, Church leaders met on the top floor of the unfinished Kirtland temple. They were washing and anointing one another in preparation for the temple’s dedication. Joseph Smith’s father anointed him, and Joseph then reported visions of the celestial kingdom. His scribe Warren Parrish wrote the account in Joseph’s journal.
passages.summary: This is a vision told in the first person by Joseph Smith. He says the heavens opened and he saw the celestial kingdom, its gate, and the throne of the Father and the Son. He saw Adam, Abraham, his father and mother, and his brother Alvin. He wondered how Alvin was there, since Alvin died before being baptized. The voice of the Lord answered him. Those who died without the gospel, but would have received it, will inherit the celestial kingdom. The Lord will judge all by their works and the desires of their hearts. Joseph also saw that children who die before accountability are saved there.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 137–138 uses this vision to teach that God offers salvation to all. What do verses 7–9 suggest about how God will judge someone you love who died without that chance?

contextNote.title: Why Alvin was in the kingdom
contextNote.text: Alvin Smith died in 1823, before the Church existed, and was never baptized. Verse 6 states Joseph’s puzzle: how could Alvin inherit the celestial kingdom? Verse 7 gives the answer: those who “would have received it” if they had lived are heirs. Verse 9 states the reason, that God judges “according to the desire of their hearts.” Verse 10 applies the same mercy to children who die young. In this passage, desire means what a person would have chosen had the chance come.

passages.title: Christ organized the righteous dead to preach to all spirits
passages.setting: Joseph F. Smith, President of the Church, reported this vision in Salt Lake City on 3 October 1918. The next day he told general conference he had received divine communications in recent months. The account was written down right after the conference. On 31 October 1918, his counselors, the Twelve, and the Church Patriarch accepted it unanimously.
passages.summary: This is a vision told in the first person by Joseph F. Smith. While pondering 1 Peter 3 and 4, he saw the faithful dead waiting for the Son of God. Christ appeared to them and preached the gospel, but he did not go to the wicked. Smith wondered how so much could be done in so short a time. He saw that Christ organized faithful spirits as messengers to teach the rest. He names many in that assembly, from Adam and Eve to Malachi, and saw Joseph and Hyrum Smith and other latter-day leaders among the dead. He saw that faithful elders continue this preaching after death. The dead who repent will be redeemed through temple ordinances.

lds.text: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 137–138 presents this vision as evidence of Christ’s reach to all the dead. How do verses 29–30 and 57 change the way you think about missionary work and temple work?

contextNote.title: How the gospel reached the disobedient dead
contextNote.text: Peter said Christ preached to spirits who had been disobedient, yet his time among the dead was brief. Verse 28 voices this puzzle directly. Verse 29 answers that the Lord “went not in person” among the wicked. Verse 30 explains the method: he “organized his forces and appointed messengers” from among the righteous. Verse 57 extends the same work to faithful elders who die in this dispensation. In this passage, the key action is organizing: Christ reaches all the dead by sending authorized servants.

events.title: D&C 1: The Lord’s preface warns the world and vouches for his servants
events.summary: The revelation opens with a voice calling all people, near and far, to listen. It says disciples chosen in the last days will carry a warning to everyone. It calls itself the Lord’s preface to the book of his commandments. It charges that people have strayed from God’s ordinances and broken his everlasting covenant. It says the Lord, knowing the coming calamity, called Joseph Smith so that “the weak and the simple” could proclaim the gospel. It says the commandments came to servants in their weakness, so their errors could be corrected and their humility rewarded. It calls the church “the only true and living church” and promises forgiveness to those who repent. It ends by telling readers to search these commandments, which it says will all be fulfilled.

events.title: D&C 2: Elijah will turn children’s hearts to their fathers before the Lord comes
events.summary: The messenger speaks for the Lord in three short verses. First, the Lord will reveal the priesthood by the hand of Elijah the prophet. This will happen before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah will plant in the children’s hearts the promises made to the fathers. Then the hearts of the children will turn to their fathers. If this did not happen, the whole earth would be utterly wasted at the Lord’s coming.

events.title: D&C 3: God’s work cannot be frustrated, but Joseph can still fall
events.summary: The revelation begins by declaring that God’s works and purposes cannot be frustrated. It is the work of men that fails, especially those who boast in their own strength. It then turns to Joseph and recalls how strict his commandments were. It says he gave in to the persuasions of men and feared man more than God. If Joseph repents, he is still chosen; if not, he will lose his gift. He lost his privileges for handing sacred things to a wicked man. Still, the revelation says, the work will go forth. It says the plates were preserved so the Lamanites might know the promises made to their fathers and believe in Christ.

events.title: D&C 4: Desire to serve is the first qualification for the work
events.summary: The revelation announces that a marvelous work is about to come forth. It tells those who enter God’s service to serve with heart, might, mind, and strength. Then it says that desire to serve is itself a call to the work. It compares the moment to a field ready for harvest. The worker who reaps with energy also gains salvation. It lists faith, hope, charity, and love as the qualities that fit a person for the work. It ends with a list of ten virtues and the promise to ask and receive.

events.title: D&C 5: Three witnesses will see the plates, but humility comes first
events.summary: The revelation answers Martin Harris’s wish for a witness that Joseph had the plates. It says Joseph covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord names. His first gift is to translate, and he should claim no other until that is finished. If people will not believe God’s words, they would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. It promises three witnesses who will be shown the plates by God’s power. Joseph is told to repent and to yield to the persuasions of men no more. Harris can be a witness if he humbles himself in mighty prayer and faith; then he may only say he has seen them. If Harris does not humble himself, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then stop until commanded again.

events.title: D&C 6: Oliver Cowdery already had a witness: peace from God
events.summary: The revelation announces a marvelous work and calls anyone who desires to reap in a ripe field. It tells Oliver to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It tells him to stand by Joseph, to admonish him, and to accept admonition from him. It reminds him that each time he inquired, the Spirit instructed him. It points him to a night when he prayed and received peace in his mind. It offers him a gift to translate, like Joseph, and gives both of them the keys of this gift. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice tells them to fear not and do good. It ends by asking them to look to him in every thought and behold his wounds.

events.title: D&C 7: John chose to stay and serve until Christ returns
events.summary: The text is written in John’s own voice. The Lord asks John what he desires, and John asks for power over death to bring souls to Christ. The Lord promises that John will tarry until the Lord comes in glory. The Lord then explains to Peter why John will remain. Peter desired to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom, and that was a good desire. John desired a greater work among men, so the Lord will make him “as flaming fire and a ministering angel” for the heirs of salvation. Peter will minister for John and James, and the three will hold the keys of this ministry. Both men receive what they desired.

events.title: D&C 8: Revelation comes to the mind and heart by the Holy Ghost
events.summary: The revelation promises Oliver Cowdery knowledge of whatever he asks in faith with an honest heart. It applies this to the engravings of ancient records. It says the Lord will speak to his mind and heart by the Holy Ghost. It calls this the spirit of revelation, the spirit by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. It names a second gift, the gift of Aaron, which only God’s power can make work. It warns that without faith he can do nothing and should not ask for what he ought not. It invites him to ask to know mysteries and to translate sacred records.

events.title: D&C 9: Revelation requires study before asking, not asking alone
events.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery to keep writing for Joseph Smith until this record is finished. It promises other records he will later help translate. It says the privilege was taken away because he did not continue as he began. He had supposed it would be given when he only asked. He must study it out in his mind and then ask if it is right. If it is right, his bosom will burn; if not, he will have a stupor of thought. It says he feared, and the time for him to translate has passed. It ends by telling him to stand fast in the work he was called to do.

events.title: D&C 10: God foils a plot over the lost pages with a fuller record
events.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he lost the writings and his gift by giving them to a wicked man. His gift is now restored, and he is told to pray always and not run faster than his strength allows. It says wicked men have altered the stolen words. Their plan is to wait for a retranslation, then claim the two versions disagree. So Joseph must not translate those words again. Instead he is to translate the fuller account on the plates of Nephi, which covers the same period. The ancient prophets prayed that this gospel would reach the Lamanites and all people in the land. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice defines his church as whoever repents and comes to him.

events.title: D&C 11: Hyrum must obtain the word before he declares it
events.summary: The revelation opens with the same call to the harvest given to Oliver Cowdery in section 6. It tells Hyrum to seek wisdom, not riches, and to say nothing but repentance. It says he will have a gift if he asks in faith with an honest heart. It tells him to trust the Spirit that leads to do good, do justly, walk humbly, and judge righteously. That Spirit will enlighten his mind and fill his soul with joy. He is not to preach until he is called. First he must obtain the word, studying what has gone forth and what is now being translated. Speaking as Jesus Christ, the voice promises power to become sons of God to all who receive him.

events.title: D&C 12: Anyone willing to reap is called, if humble and loving
events.summary: The revelation opens by announcing that a great and marvelous work is about to come forth. The voice speaks as God and calls its word sharper than a two-edged sword. It says the field is ready for harvest, and whoever reaps with might is called of God. It promises that those who ask will receive. Because Knight has asked, it tells him to keep the commandments and help establish the cause of Zion. It then says no one can assist unless humble, loving, faithful, hopeful, charitable, and temperate. It closes with the speaker naming himself the light and life of the world.

events.title: D&C 13: An angel restores the authority to baptize
events.summary: These are the words of an ordination, not a full revelation. The speaker calls Joseph and Oliver his “fellow servants.” He confers the Priesthood of Aaron in the name of Messiah. He says this priesthood holds the keys of the ministering of angels. It also holds the keys of the gospel of repentance and of baptism by immersion for remission of sins. He says it will not be taken from the earth until the sons of Levi again offer an offering in righteousness.

events.title: D&C 14: Eternal life is God’s greatest gift to those who endure
events.summary: The revelation opens with the same words given to Joseph Knight and others: a marvelous work is about to come forth. It says the field is ready to harvest and whoever reaps is called. It tells David to seek to establish Zion and keep the commandments in all things. If he endures to the end, he will have eternal life, the greatest gift of God. If he asks the Father in faith, he will receive the Holy Ghost. The Spirit will help him witness what he hears and sees and declare repentance. The speaker names himself Jesus Christ and says the gospel must go from the Gentiles to Israel. It ends by telling David he is called to assist and will be blessed if faithful.

events.title: D&C 15: The thing of most worth is bringing souls to Christ
events.summary: The revelation addresses John by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power. It says it will tell John something only he and the Lord know. John has many times wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It then answers: the thing of most worth is to declare repentance. By doing so he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

events.title: D&C 16: The same personal answer comes to a second brother
events.summary: The revelation addresses Peter by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power, and his arm is over all the earth. It promises to tell Peter something only he and the Lord know. Peter has often wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It answers that declaring repentance is of most worth. By that work he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

events.title: D&C 17: Three witnesses will see the plates by faith
events.summary: The revelation tells the three men to rely on the Lord’s word with full purpose of heart. If they do, they will see the plates, breastplate, sword of Laban, Urim and Thummim, and Lehi’s directors. It says they will see these things by faith, like the prophets of old. Afterward they must testify of them by the power of God. Their testimony will help keep Joseph Smith from being destroyed. They will testify that they have seen as Joseph has seen. The voice declares that the translated book is true. If they obey, the gates of hell will not prevail against them.

events.title: D&C 18: Building the Church begins with the worth of souls
events.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery that what he has written is true and commands him to rely on it. It says the written record holds the foundation of the Church and gospel. It confirms Oliver’s baptism by Joseph Smith and says Joseph is called for the Lord’s purpose. It calls Oliver and David Whitmer to cry repentance, with the same calling as Paul. It explains that the worth of souls is great because the Redeemer suffered for all. It describes the joy of bringing even one soul to Christ. It then speaks of twelve disciples who will take Christ’s name, preach, and baptize. Oliver and David are told to search out the Twelve by their desires and works.

events.title: D&C 19: Christ suffered so the repentant need not suffer
events.summary: The revelation opens with the speaker naming himself Alpha and Omega, Christ the Lord. It says every person must repent or suffer. It explains that “endless” and “eternal” punishment mean God’s punishment, because Endless is his name. It commands Martin Harris to repent, describing Christ’s own suffering that made him bleed at every pore. It tells Harris to preach only repentance for now. It commands him not to covet his property but to pay for printing the Book of Mormon. It tells him to pray aloud as well as in secret and to declare glad tidings. It ends by telling him to pay the printer, release himself from bondage, and come to Christ.

events.title: D&C 20: A new church sets out its beliefs, offices, and ordinances
events.summary: The document opens by dating the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It names Joseph Smith as first elder and Oliver Cowdery as second elder. It recounts Joseph’s forgiveness, his return to worldly vanities, an angel’s visit, and the translation of the Book of Mormon. It then states core beliefs about God, the Fall, Christ’s atonement, justification, and sanctification. It sets the requirements for baptism. It lists the duties of apostles and elders, priests, teachers, and deacons. It gives the exact words for baptism and for blessing the bread and wine. It closes with rules for conferences, records, licenses, and members who move.

events.title: D&C 21: The new church must receive the prophet’s word as the Lord’s
events.summary: The revelation commands that a record be kept. In it Joseph Smith is to be called a seer, translator, prophet, apostle, and elder. It dates the Church’s organization to 6 April 1830. It tells the Church to heed Joseph’s words as if from the Lord’s own mouth, in patience and faith. If they do, the gates of hell will not prevail against them. It says the Lord has seen Joseph’s weeping for Zion and has forgiven him. It directs Oliver Cowdery to ordain Joseph. It calls Oliver an elder under Joseph’s hand and the Church’s first preacher.

events.title: D&C 22: Earlier baptisms cannot replace the new covenant
events.summary: The revelation says all old covenants have been done away in this thing. It calls baptism into the Church a new and everlasting covenant that was from the beginning. It says a person baptized a hundred times gains nothing by it. No one can enter the strait gate by the law of Moses or by dead works. It says these dead works are why the Lord has built up this last covenant and church. It ends by telling them to enter at the gate as commanded and not to counsel God.

events.title: D&C 23: Five early believers each receive a distinct duty
events.summary: These are five brief revelations gathered into one section. Oliver Cowdery is told he is under no condemnation but must beware of pride. He is to make his calling known to the Church and the world. Hyrum Smith is also under no condemnation and is called to exhort and strengthen the Church. His duty is to the Church forever, because of his family. Samuel H. Smith is called to exhort and strengthen the Church but not yet to preach to the world. Joseph Smith Sr. is called to exhort and strengthen the Church from then on. Joseph Knight Sr. is told to take up his cross and pray aloud in every setting. He is also told it is his duty to unite with the true church.

events.title: D&C 24: Joseph’s strength lies in his calling, and the church must support it
events.summary: The revelation reminds Joseph that he was called to write the Book of Mormon and has been delivered from his enemies. It says he is not excused for his sins, but he should go and sin no more. After he sows and secures his fields, he is to visit the branches at Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester. If they receive him they will be blessed; if not, they will be cursed. His work is to pray, write what the Comforter gives, and expound the scriptures. Verse 9 says he will not have strength in temporal labors, because that is not his calling. Oliver is to keep declaring the gospel to the church and the world. Both men are to work miracles only when asked, take no purse or scrip, and let the church supply their needs.

events.title: D&C 25: Emma Smith is called as an elect lady with her own work
events.summary: The revelation speaks to Emma Smith as a daughter in the Lord’s kingdom. It promises to preserve her life and give her an inheritance in Zion if she is faithful. It forgives her sins and calls her “an elect lady.” It tells her not to murmur over things she has not been shown. Her calling is to comfort Joseph, serve as his scribe, and be ordained to expound scripture and exhort the church. She is to lay aside the things of this world and make a selection of sacred hymns. The text warns against pride and promises a crown of righteousness if she keeps the commandments. It closes by saying this is the Lord’s voice to all.

events.title: D&C 26: Church decisions are to be made by common consent
events.summary: The revelation tells the three men how to spend their time until the next conference. They are to study the scriptures and preach. They are to confirm the church at Colesville. They are also to do the work needed on the land. After they go west to hold the conference, further direction will be given. Verse 2 then states a general rule: all things in the church are to be done by common consent, with much prayer and faith.

events.title: D&C 27: The sacrament’s meaning matters more than what is on the table
events.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ. It says that what the Saints eat or drink in the sacrament does not matter if they remember his body and blood. It forbids buying wine or strong drink from enemies and allows only wine made new among themselves. It promises that Christ will drink of the fruit of the vine with his servants on the earth. It names those who will join him: Moroni, Elias, John the Baptist, Elijah, the patriarchs, Michael or Adam, and Peter, James, and John. It says John ordained Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery to the first priesthood. It says Peter, James, and John ordained them apostles and gave them keys. It ends by telling them to put on “my whole armor” and stand.

events.title: D&C 28: Only Joseph receives revelations that command the church
events.summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery the church will hear him when he teaches by the Comforter. It then says only Joseph Smith is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church, “even as Moses.” Oliver is to be like Aaron, declaring what Joseph receives. He may speak by the Spirit, but he must not write by way of commandment or command Joseph. Oliver is sent to preach to the Lamanites and establish the church among them. The city of Zion’s location is not yet revealed, but it will be “on the borders by the Lamanites.” Oliver is to tell Hiram Page privately that his stone writings come from Satan. All things are to be done in order and by common consent.

events.title: D&C 29: Christ will gather his elect, and Adam’s fall makes choice real
events.summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, who will gather his people “as a hen gathereth her chickens.” It forgives the elders and calls them to gather the elect to one place on this land. It describes Christ’s coming in glory, the Twelve judging Israel, and the rising of the righteous dead. Signs, plagues, and the fall of the great and abominable church come first. After the thousand years, a new heaven and earth replace the old. The text then says all of God’s commandments are spiritual, not temporal. It explains the devil’s rebellion, Adam’s fall, and the time of probation given for repentance. It says little children are redeemed through Christ and cannot sin until they become accountable.

events.title: D&C 30: David Whitmer is rebuked while Peter and John are sent to preach
events.summary: The revelation first rebukes David Whitmer for fearing man and thinking on earthly things. It says he has been persuaded by people the Lord did not command. He is to stay at his father’s house, ponder, and serve in the church nearby. Peter Whitmer Jr. is told to go with Oliver Cowdery on the mission to the Lamanites. He is to heed Oliver and pray for him in his afflictions. Only Joseph Smith is named as Oliver’s counselor in church matters. John Whitmer is told to begin preaching at once. His labor is to be at Philip Burroughs’ home and the region around it.

events.title: D&C 31: Thomas Marsh is sent to preach while God cares for his family
events.summary: The revelation blesses Thomas Marsh for his faith in the work. It recognizes his afflictions because of his family and promises they will one day believe and join him. It says the hour of his mission has come and his tongue will be loosed. He is to preach what was revealed to Joseph Smith and reap in a field “white already to be burned.” It says his sins are forgiven and his family shall live. He is to leave them only a little while, and the Lord will prepare a place for them. He will establish a church and be a physician to the church, but not to the world. He is told to be patient, govern his house in meekness, pray always, and be faithful to the end.

events.title: D&C 32: New missionaries to the Lamanites must keep to written revelation
events.summary: The revelation says Parley P. Pratt is to declare the gospel, learn of the Lord, and be meek and lowly of heart. He is to go with Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. into the wilderness among the Lamanites. Ziba Peterson is to go with them as well. The Lord says he will go with them and be their advocate with the Father. Nothing shall prevail against them. They are to heed what is written and claim no other revelation. They are to pray always that the written word will be opened to their understanding.

events.title: D&C 33: In the eleventh hour, new laborers are told to open their mouths
events.summary: The revelation calls Ezra Thayre and Northrop Sweet to hear the Lord’s word, “sharper than a two-edged sword.” It sends them to declare the gospel to a crooked and perverse generation. It says the field is white for harvest and this is the eleventh hour. It describes the vineyard as corrupted, with many led astray by priestcrafts. The Lord says he has called this church out of the wilderness and will gather his elect. The men are told to open their mouths, and they will be filled. Their message is repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. They are to keep the church articles, use the Book of Mormon and the scriptures, and be ready for the Bridegroom.

events.title: D&C 34: A young convert is called to cry repentance before Christ comes
events.summary: The voice in the revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, the light of the world. It recalls that he gave his life so believers might become God’s sons. On that basis it calls Orson his son. Orson is blessed for believing and more blessed for being called to preach. He is told to cry repentance loudly to a “crooked and perverse generation.” The revelation describes signs before Christ’s coming: a darkened sun, a blood-red moon, and falling stars. It tells Orson to prophesy by the Holy Ghost and promises to be with him if he is faithful.

events.title: D&C 35: A former preacher becomes Joseph Smith’s scribe and partner
events.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, crucified so believers may become one with him as he is with the Father. It tells Sidney Rigdon that God has seen his works and prepared him for a greater work. It compares him to John, sent to prepare the way without knowing it. He had baptized without the Holy Ghost following; now those he baptizes will receive it by laying on of hands. The revelation promises miracles to believers and says the weak and unlearned will thresh the nations. It says the gospel came through Joseph, blessed in weakness, who holds keys while he abides in Christ. Sidney is to watch over Joseph, write for him, and not forsake him. If Sidney does not write, Joseph will prophesy and Sidney will preach and prove his words from the prophets.

events.title: D&C 36: Any man who embraces the call may be ordained to preach
events.summary: The voice speaks as the Lord God and tells Edward that his sins are forgiven. Edward is called to preach as with the voice of a trumpet. Sidney Rigdon is to lay hands on him so he receives the Holy Ghost. Edward is to cry, “Hosanna, blessed be the name of the most high God.” Then the revelation widens its call to all men. Anyone who comes to Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith embracing this call may be ordained and sent out. It closes with the voice, as Jesus Christ, saying he will suddenly come to his temple.

events.title: D&C 37: The first command to gather sends the Church to Ohio
events.summary: The revelation tells Joseph and Sidney to stop translating until they go to the Ohio. It gives two reasons: “because of the enemy” and “for your sakes.” First they must preach and strengthen the branches, especially in Colesville. It says the Colesville members pray in much faith. Then it commands the Church to assemble in the Ohio before Oliver Cowdery returns. It ends by telling every man to choose for himself.

events.title: D&C 38: Be one, and go to Ohio to receive the law
events.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, the Creator, who took the Zion of Enoch to himself. It warns that the wicked are kept in chains of darkness for judgment. It tells the Saints he is in their midst though unseen, and that some are clean but not all. It reveals that enemies in “secret chambers” plot their destruction. It promises a land of inheritance if they seek it with all their hearts. It commands each person to esteem his brother as himself and gives a parable of a father who favors one son. It then explains the move: in Ohio they will receive the law and be “endowed with power from on high.” Men chosen by the Church will care for the poor and property, and all are to warn neighbors meekly.

events.title: D&C 39: A minister is offered deliverance if he will be baptized
events.summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, who gives power to become his sons to all who receive him. It defines the gospel as repentance, baptism by water, and then the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost. It tells James that his heart is right at this time. It also says he has rejected the Lord many times because of pride and worldly cares. If he will arise and be baptized, it promises a blessing greater than he has known. It calls him to preach, but in the Ohio, not in the eastern countries. It says the Ohio people pray in faith, and judgment will be stayed only if they repent. James is to baptize and lay on hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost.

events.title: D&C 40: Fear and worldly cares led a covenant maker to break his word
events.summary: The revelation says James Covel’s heart had been right, for he covenanted to obey the Lord’s word. He received the word with gladness. It says Satan tempted him straightway. The fear of persecution and the cares of the world led him to reject the word. So he broke the covenant. The revelation leaves his outcome with the Lord, to do “as seemeth me good.”

events.title: D&C 41: Disciples are those who receive the law and do it
events.summary: The revelation addresses the elders as people the Lord delights to bless. It commands them to assemble and agree on his word. By the prayer of faith they will receive his law to govern the Church. Whoever receives the law and does it is a disciple; whoever claims it but does not is not. It says Joseph should have a house built in which to live and translate. Sidney Rigdon may live as he thinks best while he keeps the commandments. Edward Partridge is to be appointed by the Church’s voice and ordained a bishop. He is to leave his business, for his heart is pure like Nathanael’s, a man without guile.

events.title: D&C 42: The law of the Church joins mission, morals, and consecration
events.summary: The revelation calls itself a law and first sends every elder except Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to preach two by two. Edward Partridge keeps his office, and no one may preach unless ordained by someone with known authority. Teachers are to teach from the Bible and the Book of Mormon, and only by the Spirit. Then it gives moral laws against killing, stealing, lying, lust, adultery, and speaking evil. It commands the Saints to consecrate property to the bishop for the poor, each becoming a steward of what he receives. Surplus goes to a storehouse for the needy, for lands, and for building the New Jerusalem. It adds rules on plain dress, idleness, care for the sick, and seeking revelation. The later verses set procedures for church discipline and for handing crimes to the law of the land.

events.title: D&C 43: Only one man is appointed to receive revelations for the Church
events.summary: The revelation tells the elders they have received a law through the one appointed to receive revelations. No one else is appointed to that gift while he abides in the Lord. If it is taken from him, his only power is to appoint another in his place. The elders are not to accept anyone else’s teachings as revelations. When assembled, they are to instruct and edify each other and sanctify themselves. They are to uphold Joseph and provide his food and clothing. Then it turns to the coming day of the Lord, when thunders, lightnings, and God’s voice call the nations to repent. It describes the Millennium, Satan bound, and the earth passing away, and ends, “Be sober.”

events.title: D&C 44: Gather the elders, convert many, and organize under the law
events.summary: The revelation says the elders should be called together from every direction, by letter or other means. If they are faithful, the Spirit will be poured out when they assemble. They will then preach repentance in the nearby regions. Many will be converted, giving the Saints power to organize under the laws of man. That organization will protect them from enemies and help them keep God’s laws. Finally the elders must visit the poor and needy and relieve them until all is done by the law.

events.title: D&C 45: Signs of Christ’s coming are promises kept, not reasons for fear
events.summary: The revelation opens with the voice of the Creator calling the Church to listen. It presents Christ as an advocate pleading with the Father for those who believe. It then repeats what Jesus told his disciples about the coming fall of the Jerusalem temple. It describes wars, sickness, earthquakes, and a gospel light that many reject. The disciples are told not to be troubled, and a fig tree parable shows how to read the signs. It describes Christ’s return, the Jews seeing his wounds, and the wise who abide the day. It then tells Joseph to translate the New Testament. Finally, it calls the elders to gather west and build the New Jerusalem, a city of refuge called Zion.

events.title: D&C 46: Gifts of the Spirit are given so that all may benefit
events.summary: The revelation says elders should lead meetings as the Holy Spirit directs. It forbids casting anyone out of public meetings. Earnest seekers who are not members may stay in sacrament and confirmation meetings. Members who have sinned should not take the sacrament until they make reconciliation. It warns against deception and tells members to “seek ye earnestly the best gifts.” It then lists gifts of the Spirit, from knowing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God to interpreting tongues. The bishop and appointed elders are to discern these gifts. It closes by asking that all be done in Christ’s name, with thanks.

events.title: D&C 47: Keeping the Church’s history became a calling, not a favor
events.summary: The revelation names John Whitmer to write and keep a regular history. He is also to help Joseph Smith copy all that is revealed. He may speak in meetings when it is fitting. He is to keep the church record and history continually. The reason given is that Oliver Cowdery has another office. If John is faithful, the Comforter will help him write.

events.title: D&C 48: Save now, because the place for the city is not yet revealed
events.summary: The revelation tells the Ohio members to stay where they live for now. Those who own land should share it with the eastern members. Those without land should buy for the present in nearby regions. All should save money and gain what they can in righteousness. That money will later buy land for an inheritance, “even the city.” The place of the city is not yet revealed. Men will be appointed to learn the place, buy the lands, and begin building. Then families will gather under the direction of the presidency and the bishop.

events.title: D&C 49: Shaker beliefs are answered on baptism, marriage, and Christ’s return
events.summary: The revelation sends Sidney Rigdon and Parley P. Pratt to preach to the Shakers. Leman Copley is to go too, teaching only what the other two teach him. It says the Shakers want part of the truth, but not all, and must repent. It restates Peter’s message: believe, repent, be baptized, and receive the Holy Ghost. It says marriage is ordained of God and that meat is given for human use. It warns against wasting flesh and against one person possessing more than another. It says the Son of Man will not come as a woman or as a man traveling the earth. It ends with signs before Christ’s coming and a promise to go before them.

events.title: D&C 50: What is of God edifies both the preacher and the hearer
events.summary: The revelation warns the elders that false spirits are deceiving the world. It says there are hypocrites in the Church who will be detected. Then the Lord invites the elders to reason together, face to face. He asks what they were ordained to do, and answers: preach by the Spirit. Teaching and receiving by the Spirit of truth edifies both sides. What does not edify is darkness, and what is of God is light. For a spirit they cannot understand, they are to ask the Father in Jesus’s name. It sends Joseph Wakefield, Parley P. Pratt, and John Corrill to strengthen the churches, and calls Edward Partridge to repent.

events.title: D&C 51: Consecration gives each family a secured portion by need
events.summary: The revelation gives Edward Partridge directions for organizing the newly arrived people. He and his chosen helpers are to assign each family a portion by its needs. Each person receives a written deed that secures his portion. If a person transgresses and is judged unworthy to belong, he keeps only the deeded portion, not what he consecrated. An agent is to use the remaining money for food and clothing. The bishop is to keep a storehouse for whatever exceeds the people’s needs. The land is consecrated to them “for a little season.” Faithful, just, and wise stewards are promised eternal life.

events.title: D&C 52: Elders go to Missouri two by two with a pattern against deception
events.summary: The revelation names Missouri as the site of the next conference. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon are to travel there soon. If faithful, they will learn where the land of inheritance is. It pairs many other elders and sends them by different routes, preaching on the way. It warns Lyman Wight that Satan desires to sift him. It gives a pattern for knowing which spirits are of God. It sends Joseph Wakefield and Solomon Humphrey east and moves Heman Basset’s office to Simonds Ryder. It tells all elders to remember the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted.

events.title: D&C 53: Sidney Gilbert is called to leave the world and serve as agent
events.summary: The revelation tells Sidney Gilbert that his prayers about his calling were heard. The voice speaks as the one crucified for the sins of the world. It commands him to forsake the world. He is to be ordained an elder to preach faith, repentance, and remission of sins. He is also to be an agent for the Church where the bishop appoints. He is to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. More will be made known according to his labor, and only those who endure are saved.

events.title: D&C 54: A broken covenant sends the Colesville Saints on to Missouri
events.summary: The revelation speaks to Newel Knight and tells him to stand fast in his office. If his people want to escape their enemies, they must repent and become humble. It says the covenant they made has been broken and is now void. It pronounces woe on the one by whom the offense came. Those who kept the covenant will obtain mercy. The group is told to flee, choose a leader, and travel west to Missouri. There they are to earn a living until a place is prepared. It ends by urging patience in tribulation and promising rest.

events.title: D&C 55: A printer’s skills are called into the Church’s work
events.summary: The revelation tells William Phelps that he is called and chosen. If baptized with an eye single to God’s glory, he will receive forgiveness and the Holy Spirit. Then Joseph Smith is to ordain him an elder to preach repentance and baptism. He may give the Holy Spirit to those who are contrite. He is to help Oliver Cowdery with printing and with writing books for schools. He is to travel with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to the land of inheritance. Joseph Coe is to go with them as well.

events.title: D&C 56: The Lord revokes commands when his servants will not act
events.summary: The revelation opens with a warning to the rebellious among those who profess the Lord’s name. It says the Lord commands and also revokes as he sees fit. It cancels the mission of Marsh and Thayre and sends Selah J. Griffin with Marsh instead. It also cancels the mission of Griffin and Newel Knight because of rebellion at Thompson. Knight is to stay and lead the contrite there to Missouri. If Thayre repents of pride and selfishness, he may still go to Missouri; if not, he must take back his money and be cut off. If Joseph Smith must repay that money, the Lord promises to repay him in Missouri. The revelation ends with woes on selfish rich and greedy poor, and a blessing on the pure in heart.

events.title: D&C 57: Independence is named the center place of Zion
events.summary: The revelation tells the elders gathered in Missouri that this land is appointed for the gathering of the Saints. It calls it the land of promise and the place for the city of Zion. Independence is the center place, and a temple lot lies west of the courthouse. The Saints are to buy land there and westward to the line “between Jew and Gentile,” as far as they can. Sidney Gilbert is to act as agent, buy land, and open a store. Edward Partridge is to divide inheritances to the Saints. William W. Phelps is to be printer, with Oliver Cowdery helping to copy and correct. These men are to settle in Zion, and the bishop and agent are to prepare for arriving families.

events.title: D&C 58: Do good of your own free will, not only when commanded
events.summary: The revelation tells the elders that blessings come after much tribulation. It says they were sent to obey, to lay Zion’s foundation, and to prepare a feast for the poor. Edward Partridge is to judge in Israel and divide inheritances, but he must repent of unbelief. The Saints must keep the laws of the land. The Lord will not command in all things, so people should do much good of their own free will. Martin Harris is to lay his money before the bishop, and he and Phelps must repent. Sidney Rigdon is to describe Zion in writing and dedicate the land and temple site. Joseph Smith, Rigdon, and Cowdery are to return home, Ziba Peterson loses his office, and others preach on the way.

events.title: D&C 59: Zion’s Saints are to keep the Sabbath with thanks
events.summary: The revelation blesses those who came to Zion with an eye single to God’s glory. Those who live will inherit the earth, and those who die will rest and receive a crown. It then gives commandments to love God and neighbor and not to steal, commit adultery, or kill. It asks for thanks in all things and the sacrifice of a broken heart and contrite spirit. The Saints are to go to the house of prayer and offer their sacraments on the Lord’s day. That day they are to rest, confess their sins, and prepare food with singleness of heart. If they do these things with thanks and glad hearts, the fulness of the earth is theirs. God is offended only by those who do not confess his hand in all things and do not obey.

events.title: D&C 60: Elders who hide their talent through fear will lose it
events.summary: The revelation tells the elders who are to return that the Lord is pleased they came. But some would not open their mouths and hid their talent for fear of man. If they are not more faithful, even what they have will be taken. The elders are to make or buy a boat and travel quickly toward Saint Louis. From there Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, and Oliver Cowdery go to Cincinnati to preach. The rest go two by two and preach on the way home, not in haste. Edward Partridge is to give them money, to be repaid by those able. Elders still coming to Zion must not bury their talent and must shake off dust only in secret.

events.title: D&C 61: Danger on the river brings both a promise and a new route
events.summary: The revelation forgives the assembled elders who confess their sins with humble hearts. It says the whole company need not speed down the river while people on either side perish in unbelief. It says the Lord has decreed many destructions on these waters, but the faithful will not perish. Sidney Gilbert and William Phelps are to hurry ahead on their mission. It says the Lord blessed the waters in the beginning and cursed them in the last days through John. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery are to travel only by canal, and Saints bound for Zion are to go by land. The three are not to preach to the wicked until they reach Cincinnati. Reynolds Cahoon and Samuel Smith are to stay together, and the revelation closes with “be of good cheer” and a call to watch and pray.

events.title: D&C 62: Testimony already borne is recorded in heaven
events.summary: The voice in verse 1 speaks as Jesus Christ, the elders’ advocate who knows human weakness. It tells the elders who have not reached Zion that their mission is not yet full. Their testimony is recorded in heaven, angels rejoice over them, and their sins are forgiven. They are to continue to Zion, hold a meeting, rejoice, and offer a sacrament. Afterward they may return together or two by two, as long as they are faithful. Those who wish may ride horses, mules, or carriages if they receive this with thanks. These matters are left to their judgment and the Spirit. The revelation ends: “I am with the faithful always.”

events.title: D&C 63: Zion must be bought, gathered slowly, and spoken of with care
events.summary: The revelation opens with a warning to the wicked and rebellious. It says signs follow faith rather than create it, and it rebukes sign seekers and adulterers. The Saints are to gather to Zion, but not in haste. Zion can be gained only by purchase or by blood, and they are forbidden to shed blood. So Titus Billings is to sell the farm, and Newel K. Whitney and Oliver Cowdery are to raise money. The revelation describes the resurrection and the separation of the wicked at Christ’s coming. It rejects Sidney Rigdon’s written description of Zion and tells him to write another. It warns against using the Lord’s name without authority.

events.title: D&C 64: The Lord forgives whom he will, but his people must forgive all
events.summary: The revelation tells the elders that the Lord has forgiven their sins this once. Joseph Smith keeps the keys of the mysteries while he obeys, though he too has sinned. The elders must forgive all men, while the Lord forgives whom he will. Ezra Booth and Isaac Morley are named for not keeping the law, and Morley is forgiven. Edward Partridge has sinned and will be forgiven if he repents. Kirtland is to remain a strong hold for five years, so Frederick G. Williams keeps his farm. The revelation calls today a day of sacrifice and tithing, and says great things come from small things. It ends by saying the Lord requires the heart and a willing mind, and that Zion will flourish.

events.title: D&C 65: Prayer asks for God’s kingdom to fill the earth
events.summary: The revelation describes a mighty voice from on high calling people to “prepare ye the way of the Lord” and make his paths straight. It says the keys of the kingdom of God are committed to men on earth. From there the gospel will roll forth like the stone cut from the mountain without hands. The voice calls people to prepare the supper of the Lamb and make ready for the Bridegroom. It tells them to pray and make known the Lord’s works. They are to call on the Lord so his kingdom may go forth. It says the Son of Man will come down to meet the kingdom of God set up on earth. The section ends as a prayer that the kingdom of God go forth so the kingdom of heaven may come.

events.title: D&C 66: A new convert is clean, but not all, and must keep repenting
events.summary: The voice in verse 1 speaks as the Redeemer to William McLellin and blesses him for turning from his sins and receiving the everlasting covenant. It says he is clean, “but not all,” and must repent of what the Lord will show him. He is to preach from land to land where the gospel has not been heard. He is not to go to Zion yet, but to the eastern lands with Samuel Smith. He is to lay hands on the sick, be patient in affliction, and not be cumbered. It warns him against adultery, a temptation that has troubled him. If he continues to the end, he will receive a crown of eternal life.

events.title: D&C 67: Elders must match the revelations or testify that they are true
events.summary: The revelation speaks to the assembled elders and says their prayers have been heard. It says fears in their hearts kept them from a blessing they sought. It notes they have watched Joseph Smith’s language and imperfections. It then sets a test: pick the least revelation and let the wisest elder write one like it. If they can, they may say they do not know the revelations are true. If they cannot, they are condemned unless they testify. It closes with a promise that the humble will one day see God by the Spirit.

events.title: D&C 68: Words spoken by the Holy Ghost are scripture
events.summary: The revelation begins with Orson Hyde’s call to preach by the Spirit. It makes his call a pattern for all who are ordained to go forth.
