Whatever they speak when moved by the Holy Ghost will be scripture. It sends Hyde, Luke Johnson, Lyman Johnson, and William McLellin into all the world to preach and baptize. It then gives rules for bishops, including the rights of literal descendants of Aaron. Parents in Zion must teach their children faith, repentance, baptism, and the Holy Ghost by age eight. The Lord says he is displeased with idlers and greed in Zion. Oliver Cowdery is to carry these sayings there.

events.title: D&C 69: Revelations and records must reach Zion with a faithful companion
events.summary: The revelation says Oliver Cowdery should not travel alone with the commandments and the money. It names John Whitmer to go with him. Whitmer is to keep writing a history of important things about the church. He is to take counsel from Cowdery and others. Elders abroad are to send accounts of their stewardships to Zion. Zion is to be the place that receives these things. Whitmer is also to travel among the churches to gather knowledge and records. The work is for the generations who will grow up in Zion.

events.title: D&C 70: Stewards over the revelations must share their gains with Zion
events.summary: The revelation speaks to Zion and to church members far away. It appoints six men as stewards over the revelations: Joseph Smith, Martin Harris, Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps. They will give an account of this stewardship at judgment. They are to manage the revelations and their benefits, not give them away. What exceeds their needs goes to the Lord’s storehouse for Zion. No one is exempt from this law, not even the bishop. Stewards over spiritual things deserve support, and all must be equal in temporal things.

events.title: D&C 71: Answer critics openly, for their weapons will not prosper
events.summary: The revelation tells Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon that the time has come to preach. They are to expound the scriptures by the Spirit given them. They are to preach in the nearby regions and in the church for a season. This work will prepare the way for revelations still to come. They are to invite their enemies to meet them in public and in private. If they are faithful, their critics’ shame will be shown. The revelation promises that no weapon formed against them will prosper. It closes by telling them to keep the commandments.

events.title: D&C 72: A second bishop must account for stewards and certify Saints for Zion
events.summary: The first revelation tells the high priests at Kirtland that a bishop is needed in this region. Elders here must account for their stewardship to him, with records sent to the bishop in Zion. It names Newel K. Whitney as that bishop. The second revelation sets his duties: keep the storehouse, receive funds, and supply the elders. Debts elders cannot pay go to the bishop in Zion, and their spiritual labors answer for them. Elders need this bishop’s certificate to be accepted in Zion, and publishing stewards may claim his help. The third requires members moving to Zion to carry a certificate from three elders or a bishop.

events.title: D&C 73: Preach until conference, then finish the Bible translation
events.summary: The revelation says the elders should keep preaching in the nearby regions until the conference. At the conference their separate missions will be made known. It then tells Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to translate again. They should also preach nearby until the conference when it is practical. After that they are to continue translating until the work is finished. This plan is a pattern for the elders until more is revealed. It ends by telling them to gird up their loins and be sober.

events.title: D&C 74: Little children are holy through Christ, not through the law
events.summary: The explanation opens by quoting Paul: an unbelieving spouse is sanctified by the believing one. It says that in the apostles’ day unbelieving Jews still kept the law of circumcision. Contention arose when unbelieving husbands wanted their children circumcised under the law of Moses. Those children followed their fathers’ traditions and did not believe the gospel. So Paul wrote, on his own authority, that believers should not marry unbelievers. His aim was to end the tradition that little children are unholy. It concludes that little children are holy, sanctified through the atonement of Jesus Christ.

events.title: D&C 75: Missionaries are paired and sent, and their families must be supported
events.summary: The first revelation tells those who volunteered to preach to go without delay and labor with their might. Faithful workers are promised sheaves, honor, and eternal life. William McLellin’s eastern mission is revoked; he is chastened for murmuring, forgiven, and sent south with Luke Johnson. Orson Hyde, Samuel Smith, Lyman Johnson, and Orson Pratt go east, and other pairs go west and south. Houses that reject them are to be left with the dust shaken off as a testimony. The second revelation asks the church to support the families of those sent out. A man who must provide for his own family may stay and keep his crown, but idlers have no place. It ends by pairing fourteen more men, including Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon, and Ezra Thayre.

events.title: D&C 76: Through Christ nearly all inherit one of three kingdoms of glory
events.summary: The text opens with praise and a promise to reveal mysteries to the faithful. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon then testify that they saw the Son at the Father’s right hand. They report the fall of Lucifer and the fate of the sons of perdition, who alone are not redeemed. The vision describes the celestial glory, like the sun, for those who receive Christ’s testimony, are baptized, and overcome by faith. The terrestrial glory, like the moon, is for the honorable who were not valiant in that testimony. The telestial glory, like the stars, is for those who did not receive the gospel but did not deny the Holy Spirit. Its inhabitants are numberless, and all will bow to Christ. The writers say they saw more than they were allowed to write.

events.title: D&C 77: John’s symbols in Revelation are explained as beings and eras
events.summary: The section is a list of fifteen questions and answers about Revelation chapters 4 to 11. It says the sea of glass is the earth in its sanctified, eternal state. It says the four beasts were four individual beasts shown to John, representing classes of beings in their glory. Their eyes stand for knowledge and their wings for power. The book with seven seals holds God’s works for the earth’s seven thousand years, one seal for each thousand. The angel from the east and the little book John ate are both tied to Elias, who gathers Israel and restores all things. The trumpets prepare the way for Christ’s coming at the start of the seventh thousand years. The two witnesses are two prophets sent to the Jews after they rebuild Jerusalem.

events.title: D&C 78: Equality in earthly things prepares Saints for heavenly things
events.summary: The revelation tells high priests in council that the time has come to organize the storehouse for the poor in Kirtland and Zion. It states that if they are not equal in earthly things, they cannot be equal in obtaining heavenly things. It names Newel K. Whitney, Joseph Smith, and Sidney Rigdon to sit in council with the Saints in Zion. It commands them to bind themselves by an everlasting covenant, and whoever breaks it loses office and standing. It names Michael as prince, holding keys under the Holy One. It calls them little children who cannot bear all things yet. Still, it promises to lead them along. It closes by promising that the faithful and wise steward will inherit all things.

events.title: D&C 79: Jared Carter is sent east again with the Comforter as guide
events.summary: The revelation tells Jared Carter to go again into the eastern countries. He is to preach from city to city by the authority of his ordination. It promises to send the Comforter to teach him the truth and where to go. If he is faithful, he will be crowned “again with sheaves.” It tells him to let his heart be glad and not to fear. The speaker names himself as Jesus Christ.

events.title: D&C 80: Where to preach matters less than what one knows
events.summary: The revelation tells Stephen Burnett to go into the world and preach to all who hear his voice. Because he wants a companion, it gives him Eden Smith. It says they “cannot go amiss” whether they go north, south, east, or west. It tells them to declare what they have heard, believe, and know to be true. It closes by naming the one who calls them as Jesus Christ.

events.title: D&C 81: A counselor in the Presidency serves by strengthening the weak
events.summary: The revelation calls Frederick G. Williams to be a high priest and a counselor to Joseph Smith. It says Joseph holds the keys of the kingdom, which belong to the Presidency of the High Priesthood. It promises blessings if the counselor is faithful in counsel, in prayer, and in preaching. It asks for prayer both vocally and in the heart, in public and in private. It tells him to succor the weak, lift up hands that hang down, and strengthen feeble knees. If he is faithful to the end, he will receive a crown of immortality and eternal life.

events.title: D&C 82: Those given much are bound by covenant to seek others’ good
events.summary: The revelation first tells the men that as they forgive each other, the Lord forgives them. It warns that all have sinned and that much is required of those given much. It says, “I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say,” but disobedience brings no promise. It names Edward Partridge, Newel K. Whitney, Sidney Gilbert, Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, John Whitmer, Oliver Cowdery, W. W. Phelps, and Martin Harris. They are to be bound by a covenant in their stewardships over the poor and the bishopric. Their work covers both Zion and Kirtland, which the revelation calls a stake to Zion. Each has equal claims on the properties by just wants and needs, and surplus goes to the Lord’s storehouse. It ends with counsel to make friends with the “mammon of unrighteousness” and leave judgment to God.

events.title: D&C 83: Widows and orphans have a claim on the Lord’s storehouse
events.summary: The revelation adds to the Church’s laws for women and children who have lost husbands or fathers. Wives have a claim on their husbands for support until the husbands die. Faithful widows keep fellowship in the Church; unfaithful ones lose it but may stay on their inheritances under the law of the land. Children have a claim on their parents until they come of age. After that, they have a claim on the Lord’s storehouse if their parents cannot give them inheritances. The storehouse is kept by consecrations, and it provides for widows, orphans, and the poor.

events.title: D&C 84: Priesthood ordinances make the power of godliness visible
events.summary: The revelation says the New Jerusalem and its temple will be built at the temple lot in western Missouri, within “this generation” of people. It traces the greater priesthood from Moses through Jethro, Abraham, Melchizedek, Noah, and Enoch back to Adam. It says this priesthood holds the key of the knowledge of God, and its ordinances show the power of godliness. Because Israel hardened their hearts under Moses, the higher priesthood was taken, and the lesser one continued until John the Baptist. It describes the oath and covenant of the priesthood: those who receive it receive Christ, the Father, and all the Father has. It says the whole church is under condemnation for treating lightly the Book of Mormon and the commandments. It sends the elders, called apostles and friends, to preach without purse or scrip, and warns cities that reject them. It assigns Bishop Newel K. Whitney to warn New York, Albany, and Boston, and ends with a promise of the Lord’s coming.

events.title: D&C 85: Zion’s record should list only those who keep consecration
events.summary: The letter says the Lord’s clerk must keep a history and record of all that happens in Zion. The record lists those who consecrate property and receive inheritances, with their faith and works. Those who do not receive inheritances by consecration are not to be enrolled with God’s people. Their genealogy is not to be kept in the Church’s records. Joseph Smith then quotes what he calls the still small voice. It says God will send one “mighty and strong” to set the house in order and divide inheritances by lot. The man who steadies the ark will fall, and those not written in the book will have no inheritance among the Saints.

events.title: D&C 86: The wheat is gathered before the tares are burned
events.summary: The revelation explains the parable of the wheat and the tares. The field is the world, and the apostles were the sowers. After the apostles died, the apostate power called Babylon sowed tares that choked the wheat and drove the church into the wilderness. In the last days the blade is springing up again, but it is still tender. Angels are ready to reap, but the Lord tells them to wait so the wheat is not destroyed. At harvest the wheat will be gathered first, and then the tares will be bound and burned. It tells priesthood holders that they are lawful heirs through the lineage of their fathers. If they continue in the Lord’s goodness, they will be a light to the Gentiles and a savior to Israel.

events.title: D&C 87: War beginning in South Carolina will spread to all nations
events.summary: The revelation speaks of wars that will begin with the rebellion of South Carolina. It says the Southern States will be divided against the Northern States. The South will call on Great Britain, and other nations will be drawn in until war is poured out on all nations. It says slaves will rise against their masters. It says the remnants left in the land will vex the Gentiles. Famine, plague, earthquake, and lightning will follow until there is a full end of all nations. It closes by telling the Saints to stand in holy places and not be moved until the day of the Lord.

events.title: D&C 88: Light, law, and learning prepare the elders to build Zion
events.summary: The revelation tells the assembled elders their prayers were heard and promises “another Comforter.” It names the light of Christ as the power in the sun, moon, stars, and earth. That light gives life to all things and is the law that governs them. The earth will be sanctified for celestial beings, and each person receives the glory whose law he can abide. A parable of a lord visiting twelve servants, each in his hour, pictures God visiting his kingdoms. The elders must call a solemn assembly, sanctify themselves, teach one another, and seek learning “by study and also by faith.” Seven angels then sound trumpets over the Second Coming, the resurrections, and Michael’s final battle with the devil. The elders must build a house of God, and the closing verses set rules for the school of the prophets.

events.title: D&C 89: A word of wisdom on food and drink carries a promise
events.summary: The opening verses address the high priests in Kirtland, the church, and the Saints in Zion. They call the revelation a word of wisdom, given “not by commandment or constraint.” The voice says it warns against the designs of “conspiring men” in the last days. Wine and strong drink are not good, except homemade grape wine for the sacrament. Strong drink is for washing the body, and tobacco is for bruises and sick cattle; “hot drinks” are not for the body. Herbs, fruit, and grain are ordained for human use, and meat is to be used sparingly. Those who keep these sayings and obey are promised health, wisdom, and strength to run without weariness. The destroying angel will pass them by, as it passed ancient Israel.

events.title: D&C 90: Two counselors share the keys and the work of presiding
events.summary: The revelation forgives Joseph Smith and confirms his keys, through which “the oracles” go to the church. Sidney Rigdon and Frederick G. Williams are forgiven and made equal with Joseph in holding these keys. The three are to finish translating the prophets, then preside over the church and school, study, and learn languages. Joseph Smith Sr. and Sidney Rigdon stay where they live, Williams needs a home, and the bishop must find an agent to clear debts. Vienna Jaques is to receive money for her journey and an inheritance in Zion. The Lord is displeased with William E. McLellin and Sidney Gilbert, and the bishop and others must repent. Zion will be chastened, yet not removed from her place.

events.title: D&C 91: The Apocrypha helps only the reader the Spirit enlightens
events.summary: The revelation answers a question about the Apocrypha. It says many things in those books are true and mostly translated correctly. It also says many things in them are not true but were added by human hands. The Apocrypha does not need to be translated. Whoever reads it should read with understanding, because “the Spirit manifesteth truth.” A reader enlightened by the Spirit will benefit, and one who is not will not.

events.title: D&C 92: Frederick G. Williams joins the United Firm as a lively member
events.summary: The revelation is addressed to the united order, also called the United Firm. It tells the members to receive Frederick G. Williams into the order. It adds that what is said to one is said to all. Then it speaks to Williams himself. He is to be “a lively member” of the order. If he keeps all former commandments, he will be blessed forever.

events.title: D&C 93: Christ received grace for grace, and so may his followers
events.summary: The revelation promises that those who forsake sin and obey will see Christ’s face and know that he is. It then quotes a record of John, who saw that Christ “received not of the fulness at first.” Christ continued “from grace to grace” until he received a fulness of the Father’s glory. Those who keep the commandments may also receive grace for grace and come to the Father’s fulness. The revelation says people were with God in the beginning, and that intelligence was not created. It defines truth as knowledge of things as they are, were, and will be, and calls God’s glory “light and truth.” Williams and Rigdon are rebuked for not teaching their children, and Joseph Smith and Whitney must set their families in order. Rigdon is to go on his journey and preach, and Joseph and Williams are to make haste also. All are to hasten the translation and study history and law.

events.title: D&C 94: Kirtland is laid out as a stake around the Lord’s house
events.summary: The revelation commands the Saints to lay out Kirtland as the “city of the stake of Zion,” starting from the Lord’s house. The work must follow the pattern already given. The first lot south is for a house for the presidency, fifty-five by sixty-five feet, with lower and higher courts. It must be kept clean, or the Lord’s glory and presence will not be there. The second lot south is for a house of the same size for printing the scripture translation. Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon, and Jared Carter receive lots and are named a committee to build the houses. The two houses are not to be built until a later commandment.

events.title: D&C 95: The Lord rebukes the delay in building his house
events.summary: The revelation opens by saying the Lord chastens those he loves to prepare their deliverance. It rebukes them for a “very grievous sin”: neglecting the command to build the house meant to prepare his apostles. Many have been called, but few chosen, and those not chosen walk “in darkness at noon-day.” The voice says the chosen will be endowed with power from on high in this house. They must tarry, as the apostles did at Jerusalem. It also names contention in the school of the prophets as grievous. The house is to be built not after the world’s manner but by a pattern shown to three men. It will measure fifty-five by sixty-five feet, with a lower court for worship and a higher court for the apostles’ school.

events.title: D&C 96: The French farm is assigned to strengthen Kirtland as a stake
events.summary: The revelation says this stake, set “for the strength of Zion,” must be made strong. Newel K. Whitney is to take charge of the place where the Lord’s house will be built. The land is to be divided into lots for those seeking inheritances, as the council decides. A portion is to serve the order’s purpose of bringing forth the Lord’s word. The voice calls the spread of that word “most expedient,” to subdue people’s hearts. John Johnson’s offering is accepted, and he is promised eternal life if he keeps the commandments. He is called a descendant of Joseph and is to join the order. He is to remove the debts on “the house named among you” so that he may live there.

events.title: D&C 97: Zion’s safety depends on a pure people and a holy house
events.summary: The revelation speaks to Joseph Smith about the Saints in Zion, many of whom are humble and seeking wisdom. It approves the school in Zion and Parley P. Pratt as its leader, as long as he abides in the Lord. Others in the school must be chastened, but the honest and contrite who keep their covenants by sacrifice are accepted. It then commands that a house be built in Zion, quickly, by the tithing of the people. The house is for thanksgiving and for instructing those called to the ministry. If it is kept undefiled, the Lord’s glory and presence will be there, and the pure in heart will see God. The revelation defines Zion as “the pure in heart.” Zion will escape coming judgments if she obeys, but will suffer if she does not.

events.title: D&C 98: Bear persecution patiently, forgive, and renounce war
events.summary: The revelation tells the Saints not to fear, to give thanks, and to wait on the Lord. It promises that their afflictions will work together for their good. It says the constitutional law that protects freedom is justified, and that honest and wise leaders should be sought. It calls the Saints to renounce war and proclaim peace. It rebukes many in the Kirtland church for pride and covetousness. Then it gives a law for enduring attacks: bear the first, second, and third offense patiently. After warning an enemy, the injured may be justified in defending themselves. It also gives an ancient pattern of offering peace three times before war, It commands forgiveness of a repentant enemy every time. An unrepentant enemy is forgiven three times, and the fourth offense is brought before the Lord.

events.title: D&C 99: A lifelong mission call, after the children are cared for
events.summary: The revelation calls John Murdock to preach in the eastern countries. He is to go from house to house, village to village, and city to city, amid persecution. Those who receive him receive the Lord, and he will speak with the power of the Spirit. Those who reject him will be rejected, and he is to cleanse his feet as a testimony against them. He is not to leave until his children are provided for and sent kindly to the bishop in Zion. After a few years he may go to Zion for his inheritance, if he wishes. Otherwise he is to keep preaching until he is taken.

events.title: D&C 100: God keeps the families while the missionaries speak
events.summary: The revelation tells Sidney Rigdon and Joseph Smith that their families are well and in the Lord’s hands. It says the Lord has many people in this region, and an effectual door will open. They are to speak what is put into their hearts, in solemnity and meekness. The Holy Ghost will bear record of what they say. Sidney is called as a spokesman for Joseph, and Joseph is to be a revelator to Sidney. It promises that Zion will be redeemed, though chastened for a season. Orson Hyde and John Gould are in the Lord’s hands. All things will work together for good to the upright.

events.title: D&C 101: Zion is chastened but not moved from her place
events.summary: The revelation says the Lord allowed the affliction because of the Saints’ transgressions, naming contention, envy, and covetous desires. Yet it promises compassion and says the Lord will not cast them off. Zion will not be moved, and the pure in heart will return to build its waste places. It describes the day of the Lord’s coming, when enmity ends and all things are revealed. A parable tells of a nobleman’s servants who neglected to build a watchtower and lost the vineyard. The lord then sends a servant to gather the strength of his house and redeem it. The churches are to keep gathering, buy land in Jackson County, and not sell their claims there. The Saints are to petition the judge, the governor, and the president, under a Constitution the text says God established. Sidney Gilbert is told not to sell the storehouse.

events.title: D&C 102: A standing council gives the accused a fair hearing
events.summary: These are minutes, not a revelation in the Lord’s voice. They record the organizing of a high council of twelve high priests, with one or three presidents. Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Frederick Williams are acknowledged as presidents. Twelve councilors are chosen, including Joseph Smith’s father, Martin Harris, and Oliver Cowdery. The minutes set a quorum of seven, a way to fill vacancies, and an order for speaking by drawn numbers. Half the council stands for the accused, and the president decides with the council’s vote or a rehearing. Traveling high priests may form councils abroad, with appeal to the high council at the First Presidency’s seat.

events.title: D&C 103: Zion’s redemption requires volunteers, means, and obedience
events.summary: The revelation tells the Lord’s “friends” how to act for their scattered brethren in Zion. It says the Saints were chastened because they did not fully obey. If they now hearken, they will begin to prevail. If not, the world will prevail against them. The scattered will return and build up Zion, but only if they do not pollute their inheritances. Zion’s redemption must come by power, led by a man like Moses. Joseph Smith is named as the servant in the earlier parable of the vineyard. He is to gather the young and middle-aged men to Zion. Pairs of recruiters are sent out to seek five hundred men, and no fewer than one hundred.

events.title: D&C 104: Everything belongs to God, so the owners are stewards
events.summary: The revelation addresses the order the Lord commanded to be organized. It says some members broke the covenant through covetousness and feigned words, and are cursed. Members are to be organized and each given a stewardship to account for. It says the earth is the Lord’s, there is enough and to spare, and the poor are to be exalted. It assigns Kirtland properties to Sidney Rigdon, Martin Harris, Frederick Williams, Oliver Cowdery, John Johnson, Newel Whitney, and Joseph Smith. The Kirtland and Missouri branches are separated. Two treasuries are created, one for the sacred writings and one for stewardship income. Members are to pay their debts and write to New York, and may pledge their properties this once.

events.title: D&C 105: Zion’s redemption waits for a prepared, endowed people
events.summary: The revelation, addressed to those gathered, says Zion could have been redeemed already but for the church’s transgressions. It names disobedience, failure to share with the poor, and lack of union, mainly among the churches abroad. It says the elders must wait “for a little season” and first be “endowed with power from on high.” That endowment is to come in the house being built in Kirtland. It says the Lord will fight Zion’s battles and accepts the offering of those who came. Those who can stay in the region should stay; those with families in the east are to follow Joseph’s direction. The Saints are to buy land in Jackson County and nearby counties, gather quietly, and not boast. It closes by telling them to “sue for peace” with all people.

events.title: D&C 106: A humbled convert is called to preside and preach in Freedom
events.summary: The revelation calls Warren A. Cowdery to be ordained a presiding high priest over the church in Freedom and nearby areas. He is to preach and warn people there and in adjoining counties. He is to give his whole time to the calling, and the text says “the laborer is worthy of his hire.” It warns that the Lord’s coming will overtake the world “as a thief in the night.” Those who are “children of light” need not be caught off guard. It says heaven rejoiced when Warren turned from “the crafts of men.” Despite “the vanity of his heart,” he will be lifted up if he humbles himself. If he stays a faithful witness, a crown is prepared for him.

events.title: D&C 107: Priesthood order rests on councils, keys, and learning one’s duty
events.summary: The instruction says the church has two priesthoods, the Melchizedek and the Aaronic. It explains their names and gives each priesthood its keys and duties. It sets out presiding quorums: the Presidency of the Church, the Twelve, and the Seventy. Their decisions must be unanimous and made in righteousness, with appeal possible when a decision is unrighteous. It traces a patriarchal order from Adam through Noah and describes Adam’s last blessing at Adam-ondi-Ahman. Then it details bishops and church councils, including a council that can try the church president. It gives quorum sizes and presidents for deacons, teachers, priests, elders, and the Seventy. It ends: “let every man learn his duty” and act “in all diligence.”

events.title: D&C 108: A troubled Seventy is told to rest and wait
events.summary: The revelation tells Lyman that his sins are forgiven because he came that morning to seek counsel. It tells him to let his soul rest about his spiritual standing and to resist the Lord’s voice no more. He should keep his vows more carefully and will be greatly blessed. He is to wait for the solemn assembly. Then he will be remembered with the first elders and ordained with them. From that time he will have right to preach wherever he is sent. He is to strengthen his brethren in conversation, prayer, exhortation, and action. The Lord promises to be with him to bless and deliver him.

events.title: D&C 109: A temple prayer asks God to accept and fill his house
events.summary: The prayer thanks God and asks him to accept the house the Saints built through poverty and tribulation. It repeats the earlier command to build a house of prayer, fasting, faith, learning, glory, and order. It asks that God’s glory and presence rest there and that all who enter feel his power. It asks that servants go out armed with power and that enemies and lying reports fail. It pleads for the Saints driven from Jackson County, Missouri. It asks mercy for nations and rulers, the Constitution’s preservation, and the redemption of Jerusalem and scattered Israel. It remembers Joseph Smith, his family, the church presidents, and the whole church. It closes by asking God to accept the dedication, with the cry “Hosanna to God and the Lamb!”

events.title: D&C 110: Christ accepts the temple and ancient prophets restore keys
events.summary: The account says the veil was taken from the minds of Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery. They report seeing the Lord standing on the pulpit, with eyes like fire and a voice like rushing waters. He declares their sins forgiven and says he has accepted the house. He promises to appear there if his people keep it holy, and says its fame will spread. Then Moses appears and commits the keys of gathering Israel and leading the ten tribes. Elias commits the dispensation of the gospel of Abraham. Elijah appears last, saying the time Malachi spoke of has fully come. He commits keys tied to turning the hearts of fathers and children to each other.

events.title: D&C 111: After an uncertain errand, the travelers are told not to worry
events.summary: The revelation says the Lord is “not displeased” with the journey, despite their “follies.” It says there is much treasure in Salem for Zion, and people to gather in due time. It tells them to form acquaintances with men in the city. It promises the city and its gold and silver will be theirs in due time. It tells them not to worry about their debts or about Zion. They should stay in the area, and the Spirit’s peace will show where. They are to inquire about the city’s early inhabitants and founders. It ends with counsel to be “wise as serpents” and a promise to “order all things for your good.”

events.title: D&C 112: The Twelve must be humble and follow the First Presidency
events.summary: The revelation tells Thomas B. Marsh that his prayers and alms for the Twelve are heard. It says some things in his heart displeased the Lord, but his sins are forgiven because he humbled himself. He is to bear record to Gentiles and Jews and keep his home in Zion. It tells him to be humble, pray for the Twelve, and admonish them sharply. The Lord says he will heal them if they do not harden their hearts. The Twelve are told not to rebel against Joseph, who keeps the keys until the Lord comes. Marsh holds the keys of the kingdom for the Twelve abroad, under the First Presidency. It warns that judgment will begin at the Lord’s house and calls the Twelve to purify their hearts.

events.title: D&C 113: Isaiah’s stem, rod, and root point to Christ and latter-day servants
events.summary: The section is a set of questions and answers on Isaiah. It says the Stem of Jesse in Isaiah 11 is Christ. The rod is a servant in Christ’s hands, descended from Jesse and from Ephraim. The root of Jesse is a descendant of Jesse and Joseph who holds priesthood and keys for the gathering. Elias Higbee then asks about Isaiah 52’s command, “Put on thy strength, O Zion.” The answer says this means putting on priesthood authority, which Zion has a right to by lineage. Zion loosing the bands from her neck means scattered Israel returning to the Lord.

events.title: D&C 114: An apostle is told to prepare for a mission abroad
events.summary: The revelation tells David W. Patten to settle his business as soon as he can. He is to dispose of his merchandise. This will free him to go on a mission the next spring. He will go with others, twelve including himself, to testify to all the world. The revelation then says some among them deny the Lord’s name. Others will be planted in their place and receive their “bishopric.”

events.title: D&C 115: A named church is told to gather and build at Far West
events.summary: The revelation addresses the First Presidency, Bishop Edward Partridge, the high council in Zion, and all members. It gives the Church its name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It calls the Saints to “arise and shine forth” as a standard for the nations. Gathering to Zion and her stakes is to be a defense and a refuge. Far West is declared holy, and a house of worship is to be built there. Work is to begin on 4 July, following a pattern shown to the presidency. Joseph, Sidney Rigdon, and Hyrum Smith must not go further into debt to build it. Far West is to grow quickly, and Joseph will name other stakes nearby.

events.title: D&C 116: A Missouri hill is named as the place Adam will return
events.summary: This section is one sentence from Joseph Smith’s journal, not a full revelation. It reports that the Lord named Spring Hill “Adam-ondi-Ahman.” It then gives the reason for the name. The place is where Adam “shall come to visit his people.” It links the site to the Ancient of Days in the prophet Daniel’s vision.

events.title: D&C 117: Leave Kirtland’s property behind, for property is little to God
events.summary: The revelation tells William Marks and Bishop Whitney to settle their business and leave Kirtland before winter. It warns that delay will not go well for them. It asks them to repent of covetous desires and asks, “what is property unto me?” The Kirtland properties may go to pay debts. The voice points to Adam-ondi-Ahman as land with room enough. Marks is to preside at Far West, and Whitney is to be a bishop at Adam-ondi-Ahman after turning from his “littleness of soul.” Oliver Granger is to work for the First Presidency’s redemption, and his name will be held in sacred remembrance. He is to come to Zion and in time become a merchant for the Lord’s people. Last, the Kirtland members are told to keep the Lord’s house holy.

events.title: D&C 118: The Twelve are refilled and sent across the sea
events.summary: The revelation calls for a conference to organize the Twelve and fill the places of the fallen. It tells Thomas to stay in Zion for a time to publish the word. The other apostles are to keep preaching with humility and patience. If they do, the Lord promises to provide for their families. Next spring they are to cross “the great waters” to preach. They are to leave from the Far West temple site on 26 April 1839. John Taylor, John Page, Wilford Woodruff, and Willard Richards are named to fill the vacancies.

events.title: D&C 119: Tithing begins with surplus, then a tenth of yearly increase
events.summary: The revelation asks the Saints to give all their surplus property to the bishop in Zion. The funds are for the temple, the foundation of Zion, the priesthood, and the Presidency’s debts. This first gift is called “the beginning of the tithing.” After that, members are to pay one-tenth of their interest each year. The revelation calls this “a standing law” forever. Those who gather to Zion must keep it, or they will not be worthy to stay. If the people do not keep it, the land will not be Zion to them. The law is to be an example for all the stakes.

events.title: D&C 120: Tithed funds are to be handled by a council, not one leader
events.summary: This short revelation follows directly from the law of tithing in section 119. It says the time has come to decide how tithed property is used. A council is to make those decisions. The council includes the First Presidency, the bishop and his counselors, and the high council. The revelation adds that the Lord’s “own voice” will guide them.

events.title: D&C 121: A prisoner’s cry is answered with peace and limits on priesthood power
events.summary: The section opens with a prayer: “O God, where art thou?” Joseph asks how long the Saints must suffer and pleads for God to act. A reply then speaks to him as “my son” and promises peace. His trial will be “but a small moment,” and his friends still stand by him. The text warns those who falsely accuse the Saints, drive them, and kill them. It promises knowledge by the Holy Ghost that has not been revealed before. It says many are called but few chosen, because they seek worldly honors. Priesthood power, it says, rests only on persuasion, patience, gentleness, meekness, kindness, and unfeigned love.

events.title: D&C 122: Suffering can teach, because Christ descended below it all
events.summary: The voice tells Joseph that the ends of the earth will ask about his name. Fools will mock him, but the pure in heart will seek his counsel. Traitors will not turn his people against him. It then lists trials: false accusation, being torn from family, prison, and a sentence of death. It pictures his six-year-old son clinging to him and asking why he cannot stay. All these things, it says, “shall give thee experience” and be for his good. It says the Son of Man has descended below them all. Joseph should hold on, for his days are known and God will be with him.

events.title: D&C 123: Record the wrongs, then stand still to see God’s salvation
events.summary: The letter suggests the Saints gather the facts of their suffering in Missouri. They should record property losses and injuries to character and person. They should list the names of those who oppressed them. A committee might take statements and affidavits and collect libelous publications. The goal is to publish the record and present it to the heads of government. The letter calls this an “imperative duty” to God, to families, to widows and orphans, and to the rising generation. Many people of all faiths, it says, miss the truth only because they do not know where to find it. It ends by urging the Saints to do all they can, then stand still and trust God.

events.title: D&C 124: Nauvoo must build a temple where sacred ordinances belong
events.summary: The revelation accepts Joseph’s offering and calls for a proclamation to the kings and rulers of the earth. It names helpers, including Robert Thompson and John Bennett, and praises Hyrum Smith and George Miller. It commands the Saints to bring their wealth and skill and build a temple in Nauvoo. Baptisms for the dead outside the temple are accepted only for a set time. If the Saints do not build, they will be rejected as a church with their dead. The Lord accepts the offering of those hindered in Jackson County and tells the Saints to build again. A boarding house called the Nauvoo House is to be funded by stock under set rules. The revelation then counsels many individuals, calls Hyrum as patriarch, adds William Law to the First Presidency, and names the Church’s quorum leaders.

events.title: D&C 125: Scattered Iowa Saints are told to gather and build Zarahemla
events.summary: The section opens with a question about the Lord’s will for the Saints in Iowa Territory. The answer sets a condition: if they will do his will, they should gather. They are to gather to places the Lord appoints through Joseph Smith. They are to build cities so they will be ready for what is coming. The revelation names a city to be built across the river from Nauvoo, called Zarahemla. People arriving from every direction may settle there. They may also take inheritances in Nashville, in Nauvoo, or in the appointed stakes.

events.title: D&C 126: Brigham Young’s long missions end with a charge to his family
events.summary: This short revelation addresses Brigham Young as a dear and well-beloved brother. The Lord’s voice tells Brigham he no longer has to leave his family as before. It says his offering is accepted. It says the Lord has seen his labor and travel for His name. Then it gives two commands. Brigham is to send the Lord’s word abroad. He is also to take special care of his family from then on.

events.title: D&C 127: From hiding, Joseph orders witnessed records of baptisms for the dead
events.summary: Joseph Smith writes to the Saints explaining why he has left home for a time. He says enemies in Missouri and Illinois pursue him without just cause. He has left his business with agents and will return when the storm passes. He says danger has been his lot all his life, yet God has always delivered him. A revelation then tells the Saints to continue the temple work with redoubled diligence. It directs that a recorder witness every baptism for the dead, so what is recorded on earth may be recorded in heaven. The records are to be kept in order in the temple. Joseph closes, unable to speak in person, and promises more letters.

events.title: D&C 128: Records and ordinances weld the living and the dead together
events.summary: Joseph Smith resumes the subject of baptism for the dead in a second letter. He revises his earlier instruction so each ward may have its own recorder and witnesses. A general recorder will then copy these certified records into a church book. Citing Revelation 20 and Matthew 16, he says what is recorded on earth is recorded in heaven. He calls the baptismal font a likeness of the grave, placed beneath where the living meet. Quoting Paul and Malachi, he says the living and the dead cannot be made perfect without each other. He then recalls voices from heaven: Moroni at Cumorah, Michael, Peter, James, and John, and others. He calls for courage and asks the Saints to present “a book containing the records of our dead” in the temple.

events.title: D&C 129: A handshake test tells true messengers from false ones
events.summary: These instructions say there are two kinds of beings in heaven. Angels are resurrected and have bodies of flesh and bones, as Jesus said of himself. The spirits of just men made perfect are not resurrected but share the same glory. When a messenger claims to come from God, ask him to shake hands. An angel will do so, and you will feel his hand. A just spirit will not move, because deceiving is against heaven’s order, but he will still give his message. If the devil comes as an angel of light, you will feel nothing and can detect him. The section calls these “three grand keys” for judging any messenger.

events.title: D&C 130: Joseph teaches that God is embodied and knowledge survives death
events.summary: In separate teachings, Joseph says the Savior will appear as “a man like ourselves.” He says the same “sociality” will continue there, joined with eternal glory. He calls the idea that the Father and Son dwell in a person’s heart false. He says angels who minister to this earth belong or have belonged to it, and God’s dwelling is “a great Urim and Thummim.” He repeats a prophecy from 25 December 1832 that bloodshed before Christ’s coming will begin in South Carolina, probably over “the slave question.” He recalls a voice saying he would see the Son of Man if he lived to eighty-five. Knowledge gained in this life rises in the resurrection, and every blessing comes by obeying a law. The Father and Son have bodies of flesh and bones, but the Holy Ghost is a personage of Spirit.

events.title: D&C 131: The highest celestial degree requires the covenant of marriage
events.summary: The section opens with three heavens or degrees within the celestial glory. To obtain the highest, a man must enter an order of the priesthood. A bracketed note explains this as the new and everlasting covenant of marriage. Without it, he may enter another degree but cannot have an increase. A note dated 17 May defines the “more sure word of prophecy.” It means knowing by revelation that one is sealed up to eternal life. The section says no one can be saved in ignorance. It ends by saying all spirit is matter, too fine to be seen now.

events.title: D&C 132: Sealed marriage endures beyond death, and plural marriage is justified by command
events.summary: The revelation answers Joseph’s question about how God justified Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, David, and Solomon in having many wives and concubines. It reveals a “new and everlasting covenant,” saying covenants not sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise end at death. Marriages made only for this world end then, but marriages sealed by the one holding the keys endure toward exaltation. It says Abraham did not sin in taking Hagar and concubines because God commanded it, and David sinned only concerning Uriah’s wife. It confirms Joseph’s power to seal on earth and in heaven. Emma Smith is told to receive Joseph’s wives and cleave to him or be destroyed; if she forgives him, she will be blessed. Under the “law of the priesthood,” a man may marry more virgins with his first wife’s consent. If she rejects the law, verse 64 says she will be destroyed, and verse 65 frees him from “the law of Sarah,” her consent.

events.title: D&C 133: Saints must leave Babylon and prepare to meet the Bridegroom
events.summary: The Lord’s voice calls on the Church to hear, for he will suddenly come to his temple in judgment. It tells the Saints to prepare, sanctify themselves, and gather to Zion, leaving Babylon behind. Elders are to go to all nations, first the Gentiles and then the Jews. Gentiles are to flee to Zion and Judah to Jerusalem, but not in haste. The revelation describes the Lord’s coming: lands joined, those in the north countries returning, and the saints rising from their graves. It pictures Christ in red garments, having “trodden the wine-press alone,” while his redeemed speak of his loving kindness. The Lord sent the gospel in plainness so the weak could prepare, and these commandments now go to all. Those who will not hear face darkness, because they rejected his servants.

events.title: D&C 134: Governments must protect conscience but never control it
events.summary: This is a declaration of belief, not a revelation; each paragraph begins “We believe.” It says God instituted governments and holds people accountable for how they make and run laws. Good laws must protect conscience, property, and life. People must sustain the governments that protect their rights, and sedition is condemned. Civil officers should punish crime but never control conscience, and no religion should be favored by the state. Churches may discipline members only by removing fellowship, never by taking property or life. People should appeal to the law for wrongs, but may defend themselves when the law cannot act in time. The last paragraph says preaching to enslaved people against their masters’ wishes is unlawful and dangerous.

events.title: D&C 135: The deaths at Carthage are presented as a sealing witness
events.summary: This is not a revelation but a written announcement and tribute, speaking as “we.” It reports that Joseph and Hyrum Smith were shot at Carthage Jail by a mob of 150 to 200 men. It records their last words and says John Taylor was wounded and Willard Richards escaped. It then praises Joseph Smith’s work, including the Book of Mormon and the revelations in this book. It quotes Joseph saying he went “like a lamb to the slaughter” with a clear conscience. It adds that Hyrum read a passage from Ether 12 before leaving for Carthage. It gives the brothers’ ages and calls them martyrs. It ends by saying their innocent blood, on Carthage jail, Illinois, and the nation, is a witness to the gospel. That blood will cry to the Lord until he avenges it.

events.title: D&C 136: The westward camp must move as a covenant people
events.summary: The revelation calls itself “the Word and Will of the Lord” for the camp traveling west. It orders the people into companies with captains of hundreds, fifties, and tens, under the Twelve Apostles. Each company covenants to keep the commandments, gathers supplies, and cares for the poor and widows. Pioneers are to go ahead and plant crops for those who follow. It names Ezra T. Benson, Erastus Snow, Orson Pratt, Wilford Woodruff, Amasa Lyman, and George A. Smith to organize companies. Then it gives rules for daily conduct: keep pledges, stop quarreling, return what is borrowed, and praise the Lord. It says the people must be tried, and calls Joseph Smith’s death needed to seal his testimony.

events.title: D&C 137: God judges the dead by the desires of their hearts
events.summary: This is a vision told in the first person by Joseph Smith. He says the heavens opened and he saw the celestial kingdom, its gate, and the throne of the Father and the Son. He saw Adam, Abraham, his father and mother, and his brother Alvin. He wondered how Alvin was there, since Alvin died before being baptized. The voice of the Lord answered him. Those who died without the gospel, but would have received it, will inherit the celestial kingdom. The Lord will judge all by their works and the desires of their hearts. Joseph also saw that children who die before accountability are saved there.

events.title: D&C 138: Christ organized the righteous dead to preach to all spirits
events.summary: This is a vision told in the first person by Joseph F. Smith. While pondering 1 Peter 3 and 4, he saw the faithful dead waiting for the Son of God. Christ appeared to them and preached the gospel, but he did not go to the wicked. Smith wondered how so much could be done in so short a time. He saw that Christ organized faithful spirits as messengers to teach the rest. He names many in that assembly, from Adam and Eve to Malachi, and saw Joseph and Hyrum Smith and other latter-day leaders among the dead. He saw that faithful elders continue this preaching after death. The dead who repent will be redeemed through temple ordinances.
